articles.title: England 26-19 New Zealand: Zoe Harrison converted try in added time wins thriller and sees Red Roses return to winning way
articles.summary: Zoe Harrison's converted try in added time saw England's Red Roses return to winning ways in thrilling fashion over New Zealand.
articles.body:
at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham @adam_j_williams

England won a thrilling contest vs New Zealand 26-19 at Allianz Stadium; Zoe Harrison's converted try in added time won it for the Red Roses who extend unbeaten run to 41 matches after draw vs Canada last week

Zoe Harrison's converted try in added time saw England's Red Roses return to winning ways in thrilling fashion over New Zealand.

Fly-half Harrison intercepted a pass inside the New Zealand 22 as the Black Ferns tried to counter her missed penalty attempt before adding the conversion to seal an epic 26-19 victory.

A crowd of nearly 60,000 at Allianz Stadium were treated to an absolute thriller between the world's top two sides, where the lead changed hands three times before the Red Roses crossed for a fourth decisive try.

England had trailed 12-7 at half-time after New Zealand responded to Claudia Moloney-MacDonald's try with scores from Amy Du Plessis and Ayesha Leti-I'iga.

But in the second half, England regained the lead when Ellie Kildunne burst clear and then Jess Breach stretched their lead to 19-12 as they took advantage of a yellow card for Black Ferns prop Veisinia Mahutariki-Fakalelu for a high tackle on Marlie Packer.

New Zealand weren't done though and levelled the scores at 19-19 when Mererangi Paul crossed with 10 minutes to play.

England looked to have missed their chance for victory when Harrison's penalty dropped short of the posts, but her timely interception was the final act and ensured England bounced back to winning ways and extended their unbeaten run to 41 matches following last week's thrilling 26-26 draw vs Canada.

September sunshine serves up epic tussle

The Red Roses came into this fixture at Twickenham having seen their 39-game winning run halted by World Cup runners-up Canada at Sandy Park seven days earlier.

New Zealand, the last side to beat England back in the 2022 World Cup final, were in fine form having won all seven of their Test matches this year so far.

It was the visitors who started with greater intent and gave England, who for the first time were benefitting from the tutelage of iconic defence coach Shaun Edwards, plenty to think about.

Winger Leti-I'iga looked to have given them the lead in the opening 10 minutes only for her try to be ruled out for a double-movement on review.

England did finally find their groove when Moloney-MacDonald crossed for the opening try from Kildunne's pass and it looked to be setting the tone.

But the Black Ferns responded stoutly. First up, centre Du Plessis reduced the deficit when she chased down her own kick forward from Lucy Packer's poor clearance and dotted down unopposed.

They would then take the lead soon after when Leti-I'iga scored just after the half-hour when she received fly-half Hannah King's clever inside pass following a burst through the England defence.

The Red Roses had to withstand more pressure before the break and were fortunate to escape falling further behind when New Zealand knocked-on inches from the tryline.

John Mitchell's side came out after the break fired up and were rewarded by Kildunne scoring a trademark try as she had too much pace for the Black Ferns to handle out wide.

After a yellow card for tight-head prop Mahutariki-Fakalelu reduced them to 14 players, Breach went over for England's third try in the corner and a 19-12 lead which looked set to be further built on.

But when New Zealand were back to full strength, they were threatening again and were rewarded with their third try as winger Paul finished off concerted pressure to make it 19-19.

Chances looked to have gone begging for both sides to win it, no more so than when Harrison's penalty attempt from 40 metres back was well short of the posts.

Instead of kicking for touch and taking the draw, New Zealand chose to run it from their own line and go for victory.

But an intercepted pass from Du Plessis was pounced on by Harrison who crossed to them be mobbed by her team-mates and lauded by a jubilant Twickenham crowd.

articles.title: Veintiséis y diecinueve años de cárcel para los acusados de matar al argentino Aramburu
articles.standfirst: El presidente del Tribunal descartó la legítima defensa
articles.summary: El presidente del Tribunal descartó la legítima defensa
articles.body: El exmilitar Loïk Le Priol fue condenado por el Tribunal de lo Penal de París a 26 años de cárcel por haber asesinado a balazos el 19 de marzo de 2022 al exjugador de rugby argentino Federico Martín Aramburu, mientras que Romain Bouvier recibió una pena de 19 años por tentativa de asesinato. Tras casi 11 horas de deliberaciones y ante la presencia de familiares de Aramburu, entre ellos su viuda María, y de los padres de Le Priol, el presidente del Tribunal, Franck Zientara, pronunció un veredicto decidido por un jurado popular y con unas penas solo un año inferior a lo solicitado por la Fiscalía. "La balística ha demostrado la voluntad de Le Priol de apuntar y tocar una parte vital de Aramburu (...) hasta dispararle tres veces por la espalda", señaló Zientara, dejando clara "la voluntad de matar" y descartando la legítima defensa que esgrimió el antiguo miembro del cuerpo de élite de la Marina francesa. Los otros dos acusados, Lyson Rochemir, la que era novia de Le Priol cuando se produjo el asesinato, y Anthony Sorrentino fueron condenados ambos a tres años de cárcel, pero exentos de cumplimiento, a no ser que reincidan. Rochemir, quien ya cumplió nueve meses entre rejas, fue declarada culpable por alteración de la escena del crimen, así como por sustracción, ocultación y eliminación de objetos, mientras que Sorrentino por haber ocultado pruebas y haber ayudado a Bouvier en su corta huida. El presidente del Tribunal tampoco dio por válida una falta de discernimiento fruto de su estrés postraumático tras sus misiones en África. Zientara apuntó a la "rabia narcisista" de Le Priol y le achacó "la muerte gratuita" de Aramburu, "de 42 años y padre de familia", al tiempo que señaló "la ideología mortífera" de la que estaba influenciado en el momento de los hechos, sin especificar cuál. Aunque los jueces descartaron el racismo como agravante legal en el procesamiento, la Fiscalía y la acusación han utilizado su pasado en el grupúsculo de ultraderecha GUD -disuelto en 2024 por su peligrosidad- para definir su perfil violento y su familiaridad con las armas. El presidente del Tribunal constató que en la sentencia consta precisamente "la fascinación" por las armas de Le Priol y Bouvier, quienes, la noche del asesinato, habían violado el control judicial que les prohibía verse tras una anterior condena. Zientara señaló que los 19 años contra Bouvier, antiguo estudiante de Derecho, se explican por haber disparado contra el argentino, quien estaba desarmado, en cuatro ocasiones. Tras esa primera ráfaga inicial que dejó al exjugador de rugby herido, Le Priol descargó su arma contra Aramburu, dos de sus seis disparos fueron mortales. El exjugador internacional de los Pumas fue asesinado después de una banal pelea regada de alcohol en la madrugada del 19 de marzo en el bar Le Mabillon del bulevar Saint-Germain de París en la que también estuvo implicado Shaun Hegarty, antiguo jugador de rugby y amigo y socio del argentino

articles.title: URC: Benetton 19-19 Dragons - Welsh side show spirit to draw in Treviso
articles.summary: Dragons draw their United Rugby Championship opener against Wayne Pivac's Benetton after Elliot Dee's late try.
articles.body:
Tries: Mey, Bernasconi, Mendy Cons: Umaga 2

Tries: De Beer, Inisi, Dee Cons: De Beer 2

Tinus de Beer hit the post with an 80th-minute conversion as Dragons kicked off the United Rugby Championship season with a draw at Benetton.

Filo Tiatia's side shared the spoils four times in 2025-26 and it was a familiar story at the start of the new campaign after a spirited showing in Treviso.

Centre Francois Mey, hooker Bautista Bernasconi and wing Ignacio Mendy crossed to give Benetton, in their first game under former Wales boss Wayne Pivac, a 19-7 lead at half-time.

De Beer got Dragons' try in the first half, and a super effort by Tonga centre Fine Inisi cut the gap soon after the restart.

Scrum-half Che Hope had a try chalked off for the visitors with 15 minutes to go, but Wales hooker Elliot Dee went over to give De Beer a shot at the lead, only for his tricky kick from the right to hit the left post and bounce out.

Dragons lose summer signing Enari after operation

Pivac, who led Scarlets to the title in 2017 before a three-year spell as Wales head coach, took over at the Stadio Monigo this summer and will feel his side should have turned their half-time lead into a victory.

Dragons will also put it down as a missed opportunity after showing tenacity to stay in the fight, but they now have a run of five games in Wales to make it a strong start.

Set-piece pressure puts Dragons on back foot

Dragons travelled to Treviso with belief, courtesy of an encouraging 2025-26 season, albeit they still finished 15th despite much-improved results and performances.

With flanker Thomas Young a constant menace, they dealt with the Italians well in phase play, but the set-piece and discipline proved to be their issue in the first half.

Benetton's pack put pressure on for centre Mey to go over on debut and their driving line-out earned a second by hooker Bernasconi.

Dragons responded well with De Beer crossing for a slick score approaching the half hour after good work by lock Seb Davies and Young.

Mistakes in handling and defence allowed Benetton to have the final say of the half through Argentina wing Mendy down the right.

That meant Dragons needed a fast start to the second half and they made one, showing an offload game that was missing last season to work Inisi in the corner.

It remained a five-point game going into the final quarter and the visitors were denied a leveller with 15 minutes to go after the TMO spotted a knock-on by Huw Anderson before he put Hope over.

Jacob Umaga missed a long-range penalty in the 74th minute to make it a two-score game, and Dragons punished the Benetton with Dee going over from an impressive driving line-out.

It could have been a spirited victory, but in the end they settled for two points, with Wales wing Rio Dyer oddly kicking the ball out rather than going for a win from the final play.

Tiatia's side have something to build on, with all five of their remaining fixtures in the first block of the season in Wales.

They now face back-to-back URC derbies against Scarlets and Ospreys in Newport.

"The mentality for the boys to say in the fight was good. We fought hard, we defended well and we took our chances. We have just got to be a little but more clinical.

"Sometimes to win games it is left on kicking opportunities, but it has hit the post.

"It could have been, but instead we take the draw and move on."

articles.title: The Prem: Northampton 59-26 Newcastle: Saints score nine-tries to beat Red Bulls
articles.summary: James Pater and Tommy Freeman score hat-tricks as Northampton kick off their title defence with a 59-26 win over Newcastle.
articles.body:
Tries: Pater 3, Hendy, Freeman 3, Coles, Sleightholme Cons: F Smith 5, Belleau 2

Tries: Wade 2, Jordan, Kok Cons: Connon, Henry 2

James Pater and Tommy Freeman ran in hat-tricks as Northampton Saints kicked off their title defence with a comfortable 59-26 win over new-look Newcastle Red Bulls at Franklin's Gardens.

Just three months after securing a second Prem title against Exeter Chiefs at Allianz Stadium, Saints were dominant against a much-changed Red Bulls side who have welcomed 25 new players through the door this summer.

Three tries each for Pater and Freeman and one each for George Hendy, Alex Coles and Ollie Sleightholme delivered an emphatic scoreline as Saints, brilliantly conducted by fly-half Fin Smith, ran in nine tries.

Yet for all that the scoreline delivered another defeat for Newcastle they still scored four tries and came away with a losing bonus point as they hope that, for the first time in five seasons, they may not be destined for bottom place in the Prem.

Carreras magic lights up Bath win over Harlequins

Ex-Saints skipper Lawes to make Sale debut - Prem team news

Will Saints reign again or new winners rise? - Prem Rugby club guide

Pater went over twice inside the first 15 minutes with Hendy, Freeman and Coles all following him in during a first period Northampton bossed.

But two tries from Christian Wade which were both converted - with the first a brilliant end-to-end and side-to-side score which had levelled matters early - showed Newcastle will cause problems for plenty of teams this season.

If those were the positives, two yellow cards were the balancers for the visitors. A first for a trip by Harrison Obatoyinbo and the second for a no-hands tackle under the sticks by Pouri Rakete-Stones hampered their defensive effort.

Those mistakes allowed Saints to stretch clear in the second period.

Throughout the 80 minutes the visitors had no real answer to the power and pace of Henry Pollock, who celebrated his new £400,000 contract extension not only with an eye-catching braided hairstyle but a performance which justified it all.

Pollock was not alone in hitting the ground running with Smith superb and Freeman and Pater ruthless.

Freeman completed his hat-trick with two second-half tries either side of Cam Jordan's first for Newcastle, after signing from Gloucester in the summer.

Sleightholme pounced just seconds after coming on as a substitute and the impressive Pater rounded off the win with his own hat-trick.

However, the impressively mobile Werner Kok scored a consolation late on to ensure Newcastle left with a bonus point to their name.

Northampton Saints' Tommy Freeman told BBC Radio Northampton:

"Good start and lots of points on the board which good to see but I think there is loads more in us which is what we said at half-time, but overall a good result.

"Our set piece we need to tighten up a bit on that first phase. Defensively we were caught a bit tight, but credit to Newcastle for stressing us in those areas but we would like to see better movement.

"It is always a challenge and going back-to-back [titles] is not done by many teams. There is a reason for that but we will be looking to take each week as it comes and keep putting our DNA on the pitch."

Newcastle head coach Dan McFarland told BBC Radio Newcastle:

"We put a lot of good stuff out there but we were tested today by a really, really good team. We know where we stand now and where we've got to work. We have a long jounrey ahead of us and that was the first step.

"It was a fantastic score when we had a length of the field try and that was really us and we also had a lot of defensive sets where we had showed really good scramble and stopped them from scoring.

"But the game is up and down. We had that yellow card and then we had three tries which were scored during that yellow, and the try just before half-time was a real killer.

"Maybe we left a couple of tries out there but there is plenty in that that we will take away and see as a real positive."

articles.title: Prem Rugby: Northampton Saints, Bath begin season with crushing wins vs Newcastle Red Bulls, Harlequins as Henry Pollock sports new hair
articles.summary: Prem Rugby season 2026/27 began on Friday as defending champions Northampton Saints score 59 points in victory over Newcastle Red Bulls; Bath also record big victory away to injury-hit Harlequins; Henry Pollock sports new hairstyle on opening night fresh from signing new contract
articles.body:
Northampton Saints 59-26 Newcastle Red Bulls

Tommy Freeman and James Pater scored hat-tricks as Northampton, the reigning Prem champions, took advantage of a favourable opening fixture to record a convincing victory over last season's bottom club.

Since the end of last season, Newcastle Red Bulls have recruited extensively and they did show signs of improvement but it was a tough ask against a side making a statement of their intention to fiercely defend their title.

Tries from George Hendy, Alex Coles and Ollie Sleightholme took Saints' tally to nine with Fin Smith adding five conversions and Anthony Belleau two.

Christian Wade scored two tries for the visitors to take his Premiership tally to 95 - just six behind the record holder Chris Ashton. Cam Jordan and Werner Kok were the other try-scorers with two conversions coming from Zack Henry and one from Brett Connon.

The opening night of the Prem Rugby season also saw Henry Pollock in action for the first time since signing his new £400,000-a-year contract , and he emerged for kick-off sporting a cornrows hairstyle.

Santi Carreras produced a wonder try as Bath exploited the absence of Harlequins' England contingent to launch their Gallagher Prem title challenge with a 33-17 victory at The Stoop.

Carreras stopped a certain try by kicking a final pass destined for Cadan Murley while it was in mid-air, darting forwards to catch the ball and then winning the foot race that began just outside his own 22.

It was a unique score from the Argentina full-back that mixed skill and athleticism and crucially it came in the 32nd minute as Harlequins looked to capitalise on the threats created by their high-tempo attack.

While Bath produced fewer thrills, they entered the interval 28-10 ahead with their line-out maul an important weapon and they also finished the stronger of the sides once Quins had run out of steam.

Marcus Smith, Alex Dombrandt, Fin Baxter and George Furbank were missing through injury, leaving Murley and Chandler Cunningham-South as the last men standing from Quins' England contingent.

articles.title: WXV: Tafuna scores hat-trick as USA edge Wales 26-24 in Cardiff
articles.summary: Wales' resurgence suffers a blow with USA edging an entertaining WXV contest at Cardiff Arms Park.
articles.body:
Tries: Bevan, K Jones, Tuipulotu, Callender Cons: Bell 2

Tries: Tafuna 3, Coulibaly Cons: Vogel 3

Wales' resurgence suffered a disappointing blow with USA edging an entertaining WXV contest at Cardiff Arms Park.

Number eight Freda Tafuna, a standout player in USA's victory over Ireland last week, bagged a hat-trick as the error-strewn hosts struggled to find the fluidity that saw them cruise past South Africa.

Erica Coulibaly also crossed for the visitors, while Wales stayed in the fight with scores from Keira Bevan, Kelsey Jones, Sisilia Tuipulotu and Alex Callender.

But the Eagles dominated the second-half, once again proving they are rising force in the women's game and living up to their status as a top-six side.

USA's winning streak now stretches to three games, while Wales must build again before they head to Japan next month.

Former Wales hooker Jonathan Humphreys saw his USA pack provide the platform for the opening try, with Tafuna breaking through a determined defence.

Wales, meanwhile, struggled for a foothold with handling errors and indiscipline creeping into their game.

A knock-on led to Tafuna's second close-range effort and while Wales were offered a lifeline when replays showed Emily Henrich obstructed a defender, referee Amber McLachlan allowed it to stand.

Wales roared back to life with a clean line break from co-captain Kate Williams. Her namesake Amy then threatened down the wing before the ball was recycled back inside for Bevan, who did well to ride a tap tackle on her way to the line.

But Wales could not keep the momentum, a knock-on from the restart gifted USA back possession and once the ball found its way out to the pacy Coulibaly, there was little Wales could do to stop her.

Wales then had a shout of a yellow card for a high tackle on Tuipulotu, but were only given a penalty, which Lleucu George just about kicked to touch.

But there was no mistaking the quality of Wales' drive, with the pack powering hooker Jones to the line to get them back in the game.

Wales were finally able to hold onto the momentum and a penalty allowed the Welsh forwards to drive deep into USA territory and with the try-line begging, Tuipulotu bulldozed over for her third try in two games.

Freya Bell's conversion hit the post which looked to have given USA a two-point lead at the break, but that was until George put in a perfect grubber kick to peg the visitors back.

Wales won the turnover off line-out ball which Callender took quickly before finishing off the try, with Wales heading down the tunnel with the advantage.

Hopes of Wales pushing on after the break were quashed early on as the ever-clinical Tafuna powered over for her third of the afternoon.

It also gave the visitors a two-point lead which they never looked like surrendering in a one-sided half.

Starved of possession and territory, Wales were not helped by their set-piece, with both the scrum and line-out creaking.

The back line also struggled to get the ball through the hands despite the rallying cries from the lively 3,367 crowd.

Moments of inspiration were few and far between with a Kate Williams try-saving tackle and Callender turnover among the few bright moments.

It was a disappointing end to the first two games of Wales' campaign, while USA will march on with home games to come against Italy and world champions England.

articles.title: The Prem: Exeter 24-45 Gloucester: Cherry and Whites stun Chiefs
articles.summary: Gloucester produce an outstanding display in scoring seven tries to win 45-24 at last season's runners-up Exeter Chiefs.
articles.body:
Tries: Iosefa-Scott, E Roots, Varney, Gulley Cons: Slade 2

Tries: Loader 2, S Atkinson, Lake 2, Joseph, Denny Cons: C Atkinson 4, Barton

Gloucester delivered an outstanding performance on the first weekend of the new Prem season to stun Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park.

The Cherry and Whites only once won on the road last term as they finished eighth, but they matched that immediately with this superb showing.

Summer arrival, and new captain and Wales skipper, Dewi Lake led the way with two of their seven tries.

Winger Ben Loader helped himself to two, while Seb Atkinson, a fine solo effort from Will Joseph and a debut try from Junior Denny completed their try haul.

Exeter finished as runners-up last season after losing to Northampton Saints in the final in June, but they were well beaten.

Josh Iosefa-Scott and Ethan Roots grabbed their first-half scores before Stephen Varney and then Louie Gulley ensured they at least managed a bonus point.

After a few years in the doldrums, Exeter had a thrilling spring and summer with their unexpected run to The Prem final at Twickenham. With new American investment at Sandy Park, hopes are high about the direction of travel in Devon but this was a rude awakening to the new season for Rob Baxter's team.

The Cherry and Whites had a miserable campaign in limping home in eighth and they have not reached the play-offs for seven years, but the acquisition of Wales pair Lake and Jac Morgan has increased belief for the new campaign.

That was in evidence in their positive start as they worked the ball from one corner to the other, with Ben Redshaw's kick bouncing up perfectly for Loader to finish.

A sustained spell of phases eventually resulted in Iosefa-Scott driving over from close range for the hosts before a smart kick over the top from scrum-half Caolan Englefield allowed England centre Atkinson to win a foot race and touch down as Gloucester regained the lead.

Loader's second try extended that advantage as he showed impressive footwork to conjure up another fine kick towards the left corner and dive over.

Gloucester had produced an impressive opening half, but Roots grabbed a second try for the hosts as the flanker found himself on the wing with nobody able to stop his charge.

However, there was still time for the men from Kingsholm to secure a bonus point by the break as captain Lake brilliantly went over in the corner after he had turned down a kick at goal to earn a 26-12 interval lead

Lake's influence in his new team was there for all to see as he was at the back of a driving maul to grab his second try for a dominant Gloucester.

Joseph then scored the try of the game with a brilliant burst of speed from inside his own half that took him outside and inside three defenders.

Varney quickly grabbed Exeter's third try and with visiting flanker Freddie Thomas sin-binned for the final 10 minutes, replacement hooker Gulley went over on his Prem debut to ensure the Chiefs at least claimed a bonus point.

However, that debut try was matched by 18-year-old winger Denny, who scored with the last play of the game to seal Gloucester's first win in Devon since 2015.

Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter told BBC Radio Devon:

"We were actually quite poor today. We didn't have a lot of ambition into the wind, we kicked quite poorly and at times when we didn't even need to - we didn't even look to counter.

"I thought Gloucester were good. They were clinical, they looked powerful at times and we lacked in composure and how we wanted to attack the game.

"We could easily have got back to having two points and two points might make a massive difference. That's why I am really genuinely frustrated because we are so much better than we showed."

Gloucester director of rugby George Skivington told BBC Radio Gloucestershire:

"We've talked a lot about behaviours and standards and what we're going after this season, but there's a really special group and we felt that all through pre-season.

"It's really easy to say but what they showed on the pitch today is a great starting point for us.

"Regardless of the result, some of the behaviours - particularly in that second half - when we were down a man and going through 30 phases of defence, bodies on the line, getting up and going again, is testament to the lads, and what they're willing to give."

articles.title: Ospreys dominated by Sharks but earn Durban bonus
articles.summary: Ospreys well beaten by Sharks in United Rugby Championship opener but earn consolation four-try bonus.
articles.body:
Tries: Hatton, M Tshituka, Giliomee 2, Bester Cons: Moyo 4, Masuku Pens: Moyo 2

Tries: Morgan, Parry, Wright, Hopkins Cons: Creighton 2

Ospreys suffered an opening weekend United Rugby Championship (URC) defeat in South Africa for the second successive season after being overpowered by Sharks.

Mark Jones' men were comprehensively beaten in Durban but, just as they did when losing at Bulls in 2025, Ospreys at least have the consolation of a four-try bonus.

Sharks led 28-14 at half-time thanks to tries by Nick Hatton, Manu Tshituka, Luan Giliomee and Lili Bester.

Ospreys stayed in the contest with scores by Luke Morgan and Sam Parry, then were right back in it when former Australia captain Liam Wright went through a gaping hole on his debut.

Sharks secured victory through the boot of Vusi Moyo and a second try by livewire full-back Giliomee, but Ospreys earned something for their spirited effort when Iestyn Hopkins went over.

Sharks have been a yo-yo side in the URC and finished 10th last season when they failed to win until round five.

It was clear from early on that they would not have to wait as long in 2026-27, even without the likes of Andre Esterhuizen, Ox Nche and Eben Etzebeth.

It took half an hour for Ospreys to get inside Sharks' 22, and that was when wing Morgan went over to cut the gap to 21-7 after three home tries.

Number eight Hatton finished off a flowing move that featured Springboks scrum-half Jaden Hendrikse three times, Tshituka went through weak tackles to go under the posts and Bulls-bound full-back Giliomee, 20, showed his exciting talent from deep.

Sharks - showing more than just set-piece power - had their try bonus before half-time thanks to Bester's score from turnover ball.

Ospreys were back in it at 28-19 with tries either side of half-time by captain Parry from a driving line-out and flanker Wright, making his debut along with fellow Australian recruits Lawson Creighton and Lalakai Foketi.

But Moyo knocked over a pair of penalties to reestablish Sharks' dominance, and player of the match Giliomee scored his second.

Ospreys still had a bonus to play for and got it with nine minutes left when full-back Hopkins finished off after a Kieran Hardy snipe.

Jones' men will need to show similar spirit next Saturday when they face arguably an even bigger test against Lions in the altitude of Johannesburg.

'We need to go up a couple of gears' - reaction

"We've come away from a traditionally tough place to come with a point.

"We were just too slow at the start. Sharks were far more excited than we were around capitalising on mistakes and a couple of soft individual collisions cost us in the first half.

"They are all fixable things that we are in control of. There was an awful lot of good to come out of the game, but we need to go up a couple of gears for the Lions."

articles.title: England 26-19 New Zealand: Red Roses return to winning ways in WXV Global Series
articles.summary: Zoe Harrison scores last-gasp try as England defeat New Zealand at Allianz Stadium to avoid a second successive draw in the WXV Global Series.
articles.body:
Tries: Moloney-MacDonald, Kildunne, Breach, Harrison Cons: Harrison 3

Tries: Du Plessis, Leti-I'iga, Paul Cons: Sorensen-McGee 2

Zoe Harrison scored a last-gasp try as England defeated New Zealand at Allianz Stadium to avoid a second successive draw in the WXV Global Series.

With the scores level at 19-19 in the 81st minute and having missed a penalty moments earlier, Harrison intercepted a pass as the Black Ferns tried to counter-attack, the fly-half diving over the line and piled up on by celebrating team-mates.

The world champions' record 39-game winning run came to an end last weekend in the 26-26 draw with Canada , but this week they were able to find a dramatic path to victory, much to the delight of the 59,871 crowd.

New Zealand, the last team to beat England in the World Cup final in 2022, suffered their first defeat under new head coach Whitney Hansen.

The Black Ferns had taken a deserved lead at half-time after tries from Amy du Plessis and Ayesha Leti-I'iga ruled out Claudia Moloney-MacDonald's opening score.

Tries by Ellie Kildunne and Jess Breach restored John Mitchell's side's lead, before Mererangi Paul's converted try drew the game level on 70 minutes.

England now travel to Canada to complete their three-Test series against the World Cup finalists in Toronto and Ottawa, while the Black Ferns play France in Hamilton.

The Black Ferns have beaten the Red Roses in all five World Cup final meetings they have contested.

Canada outclassed New Zealand in last year's World Cup semi-final to deny a repeat of what is one of rugby's great rivalries.

Under Hansen, who took over as head coach after last year's disappointing World Cup, the Black Ferns were unbeaten and have defeated Canada and France this year.

The world's second-ranked side spent a large chunk of the first half deep in England's 22, and an opportunistic kick found unmarked space for Du Plessis to dot down for a deserved try.

England comfortably beat New Zealand 49-31 in their most recent meeting in 2024, winning all three encounters since their 2022 World Cup final defeat, which has opened the door for Canada to become the Red Roses' toughest contest.

However, the years were rolled back in Twickenham as Hansen's side brought a fearsome level of physicality and speed to challenge the Red Roses.

Leti-I'iga, who had an opening try ruled out, caused havoc throughout the first half and finally crossed after Tyla King broke clear, before a poorly judged cross-field kick, with another try beckoning, let Mitchell's side off the hook.

England have not led at half-time in any of their Global WXV Series games.

Given their season only began two weeks ago against Australia, Mitchell has been quick to defend his side's rustiness.

Individual magic from Kildunne, who spotted a gap on the wing for her try, and a yellow card for a high shot by Veisinia Mahutariki-Fakalelu, presented Mitchell with an opportunity to empty his bench with momentum behind his side.

Breach's simple finish came in the next play as any fears of a first loss in four years began to dissolve.

But the Black Ferns refused to go away and continued to trouble England's defence, which is now being influenced by coaching consultant Shaun Edwards.

Mitchell's side were criticised for turning down a kickable penalty late in the game against Canada.

The opportunity again presented itself, and Harrison took it on from distance, but the ball came up well short.

Canada opted to kick the ball out and accept the draw last week, which is not in the DNA of New Zealand, and they attacked from distance in an attempt to inflict England's first loss on home soil since 2016.

That proved to be the wrong decision, as a pass was picked off deep inside the visitors' 22, and instead the Red Roses won their 14th straight game at Allianz Stadium.

articles.title: England 26-19 New Zealand: Zoe Harrison converted try in added time wins thriller and sees Red Roses return to winning way
articles.summary: England won a thrilling contest vs New Zealand 26-19 at Allianz Stadium; Zoe Harrison's converted try in added time won it for the Red Roses who extend unbeaten run to 41 matches after draw vs Canada last week
articles.body:
Fly-half Harrison intercepted a pass inside the New Zealand 22 as the Black Ferns tried to counter her missed penalty attempt before adding the conversion to seal an epic 26-19 victory.

A crowd of nearly 60,000 at Allianz Stadium were treated to an absolute thriller between the world's top two sides, where the lead changed hands three times before the Red Roses crossed for a fourth decisive try.

England had trailed 12-7 at half-time after New Zealand responded to Claudia Moloney-MacDonald's try with scores from Amy Du Plessis and Ayesha Leti-I'iga.

But in the second half, England regained the lead when Ellie Kildunne burst clear and then Jess Breach stretched their lead to 19-12 as they took advantage of a yellow card for Black Ferns prop Veisinia Mahutariki-Fakalelu for a high tackle on Marlie Packer.

New Zealand weren't done though and levelled the scores at 19-19 when Mererangi Paul crossed with 10 minutes to play.

England looked to have missed their chance for victory when Harrison's penalty dropped short of the posts, but her timely interception was the final act and ensured England bounced back to winning ways and extended their unbeaten run to 41 matches following last week's thrilling 26-26 draw vs Canada.

September sunshine serves up epic tussle

The Red Roses came into this fixture at Twickenham having seen their 39-game winning run halted by World Cup runners-up Canada at Sandy Park seven days earlier.

New Zealand, the last side to beat England back in the 2022 World Cup final, were in fine form having won all seven of their Test matches this year so far.

It was the visitors who started with greater intent and gave England, who for the first time were benefitting from the tutelage of iconic defence coach Shaun Edwards, plenty to think about.

Winger Leti-I'iga looked to have given them the lead in the opening 10 minutes only for her try to be ruled out for a double-movement on review.

England did finally find their groove when Moloney-MacDonald crossed for the opening try from Kildunne's pass and it looked to be setting the tone.

But the Black Ferns responded stoutly. First up, centre Du Plessis reduced the deficit when she chased down her own kick forward from Lucy Packer's poor clearance and dotted down unopposed.

They would then take the lead soon after when Leti-I'iga scored just after the half-hour when she received fly-half Hannah King's clever inside pass following a burst through the England defence.

The Red Roses had to withstand more pressure before the break and were fortunate to escape falling further behind when New Zealand knocked-on inches from the tryline.

John Mitchell's side came out after the break fired up and were rewarded by Kildunne scoring a trademark try as she had too much pace for the Black Ferns to handle out wide.

After a yellow card for tight-head prop Mahutariki-Fakalelu reduced them to 14 players, Breach went over for England's third try in the corner and a 19-12 lead which looked set to be further built on.

But when New Zealand were back to full strength, they were threatening again and were rewarded with their third try as winger Paul finished off concerted pressure to make it 19-19.

Chances looked to have gone begging for both sides to win it, no more so than when Harrison's penalty attempt from 40 metres back was well short of the posts.

Instead of kicking for touch and taking the draw, New Zealand chose to run it from their own line and go for victory.

But an intercepted pass from Du Plessis was pounced on by Harrison who crossed to them be mobbed by her team-mates and lauded by a jubilant Twickenham crowd.

articles.title: WXV Global Series: Australia come from behind to overpower Scotland
articles.summary: Scotland suffer a third successive defeat in the WXV Global Series as clinical Australia prove too strong in Edinburgh.
articles.body:
Tries : Gallagher Cons : Nelson Pens : Nelson

Tries : Miller, Wood, Hoy, Moleko Cons : Wood 2 Pens : Wood 2

Scotland suffered a third successive defeat in the WXV Global Series as clinical Australia proved too strong in Edinburgh.

After losses against Canada and New Zealand - ranked two and three in the world - hopes were high the Scots could get off the mark against the side one place below them in the world rankings.

Despite leading 10-5 at the break, Scotland could not live with the rampant Wallaroos, who ran in three tries in a devastating eight-minute second-half spell to secure a comfortable win.

The sides meet again in Sydney next weekend.

Evie Gallagher, following her two tries against New Zealand last weekend, gave Scotland the lead on 15 minutes, dotting down to round off a period of pressure on the Australian line.

The hosts were on top, with Meryl Smith in midfield and lock Holland Bogan carrying hard and asking questions of the Australian defence, but loose work at the line-out cost Dave Butcher's team some promising attacking positions.

The Wallaroos grew into the game as the half wore on and hit back with a well-worked try. Scotland repelled a rolling line-out maul close to their own line, but the visitors remained patient and spun the ball wide for Georgina Friedrichs to put Desiree Miller over in the corner.

The Scots hit back immediately when Australia were penalised for holding on straight from the restart, and Helen Nelson banged over a penalty to give her side a five-point lead at the break.

However, Australia flew out of the blocks after the interval and turned the game on its head with three tries in quick succession.

The first came when a rolling line-out maul was halted just short and scrum-half Samantha Wood was on hand to dive over. She converted her own try to nudge the visitors in front for the first time, and it was a double blow for Scotland as Gallagher was sin-binned for illegally bringing down the initial maul.

With the numerical advantage, the Wallaroos came on strong as Brianna Hoy and then Faitala Moleko cut through to score and put the visitors in charge at 24-10.

Wood knocked over a penalty to put Australia beyond two scores and added another late on to cap off a dominant second half from the Wallaroos.

articles.title: Gallagher Prem: Gloucester upset Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park as Bristol Bears beat Sale Sharks in Country Lawes homecoming
articles.summary: Round-up from the Gallagher Prem as Gloucester upset Exeter Chiefs for first win in Devon since 2015, while Bristol Bears beat Sale Sharks in Courtney Lawes' first domestic game in England in two years
articles.body:
New-look Gloucester got their season off to a cracking start with an emphatic 45-24 bonus-point victory over last season's beaten Prem finalists Exeter at Sandy Park.

Inspired by impressive summer arrivals Dewi Lake, Jac Morgan and Jean Kleyn, it was Gloucester's first league win on Devon soil since 2015.

Exeter, ravaged by illness on top of the squad absences they already had, looked out of sorts for large parts of the game and only in the closing stages, once the outcome was beyond doubt, did they look more like their usual selves.

A beautifully judged kick-pass by full-back Ben Redshaw created a try after only five minutes for winger Ben Loader, but Exeter responded with an intense period of pressure which resulted in tight-head prop Josh Iosefa-Scott burrowing over from close range, converted by Henry Slade.

However, more clever kicking from the Cherry and Whites, this time with an excellent chip over the defence by scrum-half Caolan Englefield, served up a touchdown for England centre Seb Atkinson.

Fly-half Charlie Atkinson added a conversion and to another try by Loader, his second of the game, after the former's excellent crossfield kick found the wide man.

England A back rower Ethan Roots went on a barnstorming run down the left-hand touchline to score after Greg Fisilau's initial break.

Exeter criminally gave away a soft penalty from the restart, Gloucester kicked to the corner and skipper and hooker Lake popped up with the ball from the driving maul to dot down in the corner for the bonus-point try, with Charlie Atkinson converting superbly from the touchline to give a 14-point lead at the interval.

It took only six minutes of the second half for Welsh international Lake to turn his contribution into a brace, and Gloucester all but wrapped the game up on the hour mark with a brilliant individual score from winger Will Joseph, who ran from halfway, skipping away from tackles to ground the ball under the uprights, with Charlie Atkinson converting.

Exeter hit back with Italian international scrum-half Stephen Varney racing away to cross against his old club and Slade improving the score for a 38-19 deficit.

A Redshaw tackle denied Varney a second try soon after, and even after blindside flanker Freddie Thomas was yellow-carded for an infringement close to his own line, Gloucester's defence held firm once again.

The Chiefs managed to salvage something with a bonus-point score four minutes from time, with replacement hooker Louie Gulley rounding off a training-ground move on his Prem debut from a five-metre lineout, only for Junior Denny to add a seventh for Gloucester to end it.

Courtney Lawes' Sale debut ended in defeat as Bristol ran in five tries to open their Prem Rugby campaign with an entertaining 34-24 win in Salford.

The 37-year-old England great made his first appearance in the competition since he led Northampton to the title at Twickenham in 2024 but it was Pat Lam's Bears who took the spoils.

Bristol forced the early pressure but former Sale fly-half AJ MacGinty missed a relatively straightforward penalty early on.

From there Sale began to enjoy a period of pressure which culminated in Cowan-Dickie squeezing over from close range inside the right channel after good work from Roe moments earlier, with George Ford added the conversion to make it 7-0 before Bristol came back and had a try from full-back Tom Jordan ruled out following a quickly taken lineout.

But the Bears claimed their first try in the 12th minute when James Williams' long pass found Rees-Zammit and the Wales international dived over in the right corner.

Ford then booted a penalty for Sale but Rees-Zammit had his second try for Bristol in the 23rd minute after taking a pass from Jordan and crossing in the right corner again.

A minute before the interval, the visitors scored their third try when scrum-half Randall collected possession and dived over from close range.

Williams, who had scored a penalty in the 31st minute, then converted Randall's try to give Bristol a 20-10 interval lead.

Early in the second half, Sale winger O'Flaherty raced clear to score in the right corner and Ford's second conversion cut Bristol's lead to three points.

After a period of pressure on Sale's line, Bristol had their fourth try in the 57th minute when Randall sniped over the line from close range.

O'Flaherty finished well again for his second but Gwilliam powered over from close range for Bristol's fifth and Williams added his third conversion to leave Sale empty-handed.

articles.title: Super League play-off semi-final: Wigan Warriors 6-33 Wakefield Trinity - Wakefield reach Grand Final
articles.summary: Wakefield Trinity produce a sensational upset to reach their first ever Super League Grand Final and end Wigan Warriors' hopes of a treble in 2026.
articles.body:
Betfred Super League play-off semi-final

Tries: Johnstone 2, Sinfield, Hall, Rodwell Goals: Jowitt 6 Drop-goal: Lino

Wakefield Trinity produced a sensational upset to reach their first ever Super League Grand Final and end Wigan Warriors' hopes of a treble in 2026.

Having led 8-6 at the end of a tight first period, the visitors took full advantage of Adam Keighran's second-half yellow card, with Tom Johnstone, Jack Sinfield and Corey Hall all crossing while the Wigan centre was in the sin-bin.

England winger Johnstone had earlier replied to Brad O'Neill's opener for the Warriors and Ky Rodwell added Wakefield's fifth try as Trinity registered 33 unanswered points to book their spot at Old Trafford.

A Championship side as recently as 2024, Wakefield have made huge progress in recent seasons under ambitious owner Matt Ellis and experienced head coach Daryl Powell - and they are now just one win away from becoming Super League champions.

They will face Warrington Wolves in the title decider on Saturday, 3 October.

Wigan went into the play-off semi-final on a 16-game winning run and with two trophies - the Challenge Cup and the League Leaders' Shield - already secured.

However, their hopes of getting to a fourth consecutive Grand Final were crushed on home soil by an outstanding Wakefield display.

'Pipe dream' to reality? Wakefield reach Grand Final

Relive Wakefield's semi-final win over Wigan

Warrington edge past Leeds to reach Grand Final

Wigan's only points came while Wakefield forward Jezz Tevaga was in the sin-bin for a trip on Liam Marshall, but it was Keighran's yellow card for a late tackle on Isaiah Vagana that proved to be the pivotal moment.

Wakefield's lead stretched from two points to 18 during Keighran's spell off the field, much to the delight of the away supporters stationed behind the end they were attacking.

Mason Lino's drop-goal and Max Jowitt's second penalty of the match added further gloss to the scoreline, and owner Ellis joined the celebrations on the field at full-time.

Only five clubs have won Grand Finals since the first was staged in 1998; Wigan, St Helens, Bradford Bulls, Leeds Rhinos and Hull KR.

Wakefield's win guarantees there will be a sixth name on the trophy and a new champion for the second successive year, following Rovers' victory in 2025.

Warrington have lost all four previous Grand Finals in which they have appeared, the most recent of them in 2018.

Powell, who was in charge of Castleford Tigers when they lost the Grand Final in 2017, is sure to be a central figure in the build-up, given his unspectacular season-and-a-half spell in charge of the Wolves which ended midway through the 2023 campaign.

Meanwhile, try-scoring half-back Sinfield is set to play in a Grand Final 11 years after his father, Sir Kevin Sinfield, made the last of his eight Grand Final appearances.

Sir Kevin won seven titles with Leeds Rhinos and he is scheduled to deliver the match ball before next Saturday's game to round off his latest fundraising effort for motor neurone disease (MND) charities.

"Hopefully he'll be there!" Jack Sinfield told BBC Two. "He's not here tonight because he's starting in the morning, but I'm sure he'll be watching and I can't wait to see him next week.

"I've been there [to Grand Finals] a fair few times watching so it will be nice to do it the other way round and he can hopefully watch me win one."

articles.title: The Prem: Sale 24-34 Bristol: Bears put down marker with win at Sharks
articles.summary: Bristol Bears claim a notable win away against Sale Sharks, running in five tries in a 34-24 success at CorpAcq Stadium.
articles.body:
Tries: Cowan-Dickie, O'Flaherty 2 Cons: Ford 3 Pen: Ford

Tries: Rees-Zammit 2, Randall 2, Gwilliam Cons: Williams 3 Pen: Williams

Bristol Bears got their Prem campaign off to a fine start as they claimed a bonus-point triumph away to Sale Sharks.

With no newcomers in their starting line-up, Bristol showed the benefit of continuity as they ran in five tries to get up and running in style.

Wales star Louis Rees-Zammit got two of them, Harry Randall matched that with scores either side of half-time, before a 73rd-minute effort from replacement hooker Tomas Gwilliam made certain of victory.

But it was a disappointing first night for the Sharks, who lost no fewer than 13 Prem games last season.

Luke Cowan-Dickie's try had put them ahead early on and Tom O'Flaherty scored two in the second half but they finished short of either of the bonus point markers.

Few Prem sides probably have as much to prove this season as Sale after their run of three successive play-off finishes was emphatically ended by a disappointing seventh place, and they also had a losing home record at CorpAcq Stadium.

They have brought back big names Courtney Lawes and Joe Marchant from France to add more substance as they bid to get back into top-four contention, but this was not a good way to start for Alex Sanderson's team.

The Bears were only one place, but 18 points, above their opponents in the final table in June although their last campaign was undermined by a raft of injuries.

That curse is already strong again this term with new signing from Bath, Ethan Staddon, suffering an ACL. But for director of rugby Pat Lam having a number of senior players back at his disposal has provided the freshness akin to that of new signings.

Fly-half MacGinty picked a severe Achilles injury in the opening game 12 months ago and did not play again last season. The USA international should have got the score moving on his return with an early penalty, only to pull his effort badly wide of the sticks - much to his own disgust.

That came back to haunt the visitors as Cowan-Dickie went over

Bristol thought they had responded when some smart opportunism from Rees-Zammit - in taking a quick lineout after the ball had squirmed past Tom O'Flaherty - put Scotland full-back Tom Jordan over, but that was ruled out as Sharks winger O'Flaherty had not touched the ball.

Rees-Zammit did get his try moments later after a big floated pass from James Williams gave him an easy finish.

A George Ford penalty pushed Sale's advantage to five points, but Rees-Zammit's second try brought his side level when he produced an acrobatic finish from Jordan's zipped pass.

James Williams' three-pointer had Bristol ahead and some fine sniping from scrum-half Randall saw him burrow over to give his side a 10-point cushion at the break.

O'Flaherty produced a nice finish to quickly bring Sale back into things in the second half but despite some belligerent home defending near their own line, Randall grabbed his second of the game.

A thrilling break from explosive Fiji back-row forward Elia Canakaivata on his Prem debut broke open the play and although he was brought down, O'Flaherty eventually finished off the move and it was a three-point game heading into the final 10 minutes.

But the Bears forwards produced the decisive move of the game as their driving maul overpowered their opponents with Gwilliam the man to get the ball down.

Sale tried to respond to the restored 10-point deficit but when Ford missed a penalty in the 79th minute, their hopes of a losing bonus-point and clawing their way back to parity had gone.

Bristol Bears director of rugby Pat Lam told BBC Radio Bristol:

"I'm pleased for the guys because they got some evidence of what they put into pre-season.

"Everyone wants to be better every day and they got their rewards for it. It gives them a lot of confidence heading into next week.

(On what pleased him most): "The workrate. Defensively yes, there's physicality but one area we've really worked on is boys getting back in the game and really helping their mates. That's an area we continue to work on, but we won the physical battle today."

articles.title: WXV Global Series: Lynn still positive despite Wales' USA setback
articles.summary: Head coach Sean Lynn is still seeing the positives despite Wales' narrow WXV defeat to USA.
articles.body:
Head coach Sean Lynn says he is still seeing the positives despite Wales' narrow WXV defeat to USA.

Wales had gone into the game full of confidence after their eight-try mauling of South Africa, but failed to produce a repeat performance in front of the Cardiff Arms Park faithful.

The first half was encouraging enough, with Wales clawing back a 14-point deficit, but hopes of a second-half resurgence were short-lived amid a string of individual errors that allowed The Eagles to emerge 26-24 winners.

But as Wales head into their week off ahead of next month's double-header against Japan, Lynn said he has seen enough progress.

"I saw some grit, I saw some effort there," he told BBC Sport.

"Before, when we were 21-7 down, I would have seen heads drop, but we're in a good place and came back. Now it's about us learning how to see games off and going back to the simple things we're doing well."

USA edge past Wales in WXV with Tafuna hat-trick

As it happened: USA earn slender WXV series win over Wales

Lynn had hopes of making it three wins on the bounce after the summer's victory over the Barbarians, but saw Wales fall agonisingly short against a side ranked five places above them at sixth in the world.

"When we came into it [pre-season] at the start of July, we said we're going to be a competitive 80-minute team... we did that today," he said.

"Shame we just didn't come up with the penalty, maybe at the end, but we needed to be better elsewhere around the park.

"We need to look at ourselves and individual errors; we can't play Test match rugby if we make those individual errors, and we all know that.

"We just couldn't keep the ball; we had opportunities to get out of our 22, we had opportunities to go into their 22 and put pressure on."

Wales co-captain Kate Williams was in tears of joy last week, but said the team was "deflated" after their USA showing.

"As a team, we were there at the 60th minute; we just needed to execute and we didn't," she said.

"What happens then is you're just looking at each other, because it's a mistake here, a mistake there; we just needed to come together and do what we're good at, which is being physical and taking it to them.

"This might sound like a big statement, but it didn't feel like a game that they out and out won against us; it felt like a game that we lost, and that's just really frustrating."

Wales will have a week to reflect on such frustrations before returning to camp to prepare for next month's trip to Japan, where they face the Sakura Fifteen in two Tests on 24 and 31 October.

articles.title: England embrace growing competitiveness of women's rugby
articles.summary: England edge past New Zealand with a last-gasp try by Zoe Harrison as they embrace the growing competitiveness of women's rugby.
articles.body:
Winning had been the only currency known to John Mitchell's Red Roses.

From his arrival midway through the 2023 WXV1 campaign to winning the Women's Rugby World Cup for the first time in 11 years, England won every single game.

However, their record 39-game run of victories was finally halted by Canada, last year's World Cup finalists, in a thrilling 26-26 draw at Sandy Park last week.

Welcoming New Zealand, unbeaten under new head coach Whitney Hansen, to Allianz Stadium brought a feeling of jeopardy that had not been felt for a very long time.

Despite Mitchell openly stating that the WXV Global Series, with no trophy at the end of it, would provide new opportunities, losing in front of a 59,871 crowd at the home of English rugby would not have been part of the long-term development plan.

When Braxton Sorensen-McGee, with less than 10 minutes remaining, landed a tough conversion to bring the Black Ferns level at 19-19, the Red Roses once again found themselves in a sticky situation.

Unlike last week, they came up clutch as Zoe Harrison redeemed herself for a late penalty miss by snatching victory with an intercept try in the final play.

Given the clock was in overtime, England do have to count themselves lucky that New Zealand attempted to run from deep and gifted them a winning score.

"We couldn't have a repeat of what happened against Canada last week. A draw wasn't good enough, so we had to get the points somehow," Harrison told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"It's massive - it goes back to that World Cup final [in 2022] for me - beating them on home soil was fantastic and it being such a close game is great for women's rugby."

Rugby Union Weekly: Harrison's last-gasp try seals dramatic England win

'Important to learn how to win tight Test matches'

New Zealand, the world's second-ranked side, remain the last team to defeat the Red Roses at the World Cup final in 2022.

Leading 12-7 at half-time, ending that unbeaten run looked a real possibility.

This campaign, England have lacked the same clinical edge that saw them become world champions.

Their defence, now supported by coaching legend Shaun Edwards, has also been leaky. But they are without a number of key players, including World Cup-winning captain Zoe Stratford.

"To put it into context, the Red Roses don't play New Zealand and Canada often - it's important to learn how to win tight Test matches," Mitchell said.

"The message at half-time was that this game will turn - we will get some possession and let's attack it.

"The girls took the handbrake off and tried to go to space, even from deep, and were still tenacious without the ball, which was awesome."

Running from 2026 to 2028, the new WXV Global Series features the world's top 12 teams and is designed to provide more competitive matches before the 2029 World Cup.

England have already faced the world's second and third-ranked sides and now travel to Canada to complete their three-Test series against the World Cup runners-up.

"The game is getting better and better and we are just trying to make that gap bigger," Red Roses captain Meg Jones said.

"We know there are going to be close games and we will compete as hard as we can."

New Zealand have beaten England in five World Cup finals and were once the undisputed number one team in the world.

That dominance has faded in recent years, particularly after their failure to reach last year's World Cup final.

Despite a fourth straight defeat by the Red Roses, it is clear under Hansen that the Black Ferns are trending in the right direction.

That comes after increased investment in the domestic game, with Super Rugby Aupiki operating as a fully professional, full-time competition for the first time this year.

"We didn't want a draw," New Zealand head coach Whitney Hansen said.

"After watching last week [against Canada], we knew we were going to fight to the death, so I love that she threw that pass.

"I think for us, win or lose, we're about our performance. We've talked heaps about what does great look like - where have we achieved that and where haven't we?"

Next year, the British and Irish Lions women's team will tour New Zealand for the first time.

A competitive series is essential to the success of the tour.

Prior to last year's epic finale at Allianz Stadium, England - likely to make up a large portion of the Lions squad - comfortably beat New Zealand 49-31 in their most recent meeting in 2024.

"People are starting to realise the context we are in. Even if we had lost, we were right up there," Mitchell added.

"New Zealand are in a really great position for the Lions series and heading in the right direction for the [2027] World Cup. We are also evolving [as a team]."

Blowing away every team comfortably or being pushed to the limit to win a Test - which would England prefer?

"This is what living feels like," Jones declared.

Games in October against Toronto and Ottawa, with the series perfectly poised at 1-1, should give them those feelings again.

This was only the third game of the season for Mitchell's players, but being pushed all the way is something that he and his side are loving and embracing.

Despite all that, an undefeated run spanning four years has been extended further.

articles.title: URC: Scarlets 15-21 Cardiff - Visitors celebrate first Welsh derby win of the season
articles.summary: Cardiff triumph in the first United Rugby Championship (URC) Welsh derby of the season by beating Scarlets in Llanelli.
articles.body:
Tries: Roberts, Murray Cons: Anscombe Pens: Hawkins

Tries: D Thomas, Basham, E Lloyd Cons: Sheedy 2, Evans

Cardiff triumphed in the first United Rugby Championship (URC) Welsh derby of the season by beating Scarlets in Llanelli.

Tries from flanker Dan Thomas, player-of-the-match Taine Basham and replacement hooker Evan Lloyd helped seal the victory, with all three tries coming from effective attacking driving line-outs.

Scarlets scored first-half tries through centre Joe Roberts and full-back Blair Murray but could only manage a second-half penalty from Joe Hawkins.

Wales centre Eddie James starred for Scarlets, but he could not inspire a home victory.

It was a match played in front of a crowd of 7,073 after kicking off at the unfriendly time of quarter to eight on a Saturday evening.

Elias reaches 200 but can't celebrate with victory

Cardiff, who finished sixth last season and were the only Welsh team to reach the play-offs, were without injured Wales wing Josh Adams but gave debuts to summer signings former Australia prop Scott Sio and Namibia centre Le Roux Malan.

Scarlets, who were 14th in the 2025-26 campaign with only Dragons and Zebre below them, were missing injured number eights Fletcher Anderson and Taine Plumtree, and Wales fly-half Sam Costelow.

Wales props Corey Domachowski and Kemsley Mathias were also absent, as the hosts were led out by vice-captain Ryan Elias, who was making his 200th appearance.

It was the hosts who drew first blood with a superb break from scrum-half Dane Blacker and a neat offload from flanker Sam Lousi releasing Roberts.

Cardiff struck back with a more methodical try as flanker Thomas was driven over from an effective maul.

Scarlets again demonstrated why they looked more dangerous in possession during the first half when Murray scored a fine individual try after being expertly put through a gap by centre James, who showed the deft side in his armoury alongside the power game.

James has been employed as an outside centre by national head coach Steve Tandy but proved against Cardiff why he is a more natural inside centre with his powerful ball-carrying display.

Cardiff defence coach Gethin Jenkins would have been unimpressed by the effortless manner in which Murray glided through the visitors' defence.

Cardiff did not panic, though, and Basham powered over as the visitors led 14-12 at half-time.

In the early second-half exchanges, Murray again showed his threat as a runner, while fly-half Callum Sheedy almost created a chance for Cardiff by cheekily heading the ball after following up his kick.

Sheedy's opposite number Gareth Anscombe had made his competitive debut before he was replaced early in the second half by Joe Hawkins, who made an immediate impression by slotting over a penalty for Scarlets to regain the lead.

Another Wales fly-half, Jarrod Evans, who returned to Cardiff from Harlequins, was introduced among a raft of replacements that included Wales flanker James Botham with the bench proving crucial in the second-half success.

After a lovely sunny day in Llanelli, both sides were treated to driving rain before Scarlets wing Ellis Mee lifted the home crowd by forcing a penalty with an effective tackle and jackal.

Murray's pinpoint kick almost set up an encouraging attacking platform for Scarlets but was deemed to have gone out on the full after hitting the touchline, with referee Adam Jones consulting the television match official (TMO).

This proved a pivotal moment because Cardiff were handed an offensive position and made no mistake with replacement hooker Lloyd diving over.

Evans converted before missing a long-range penalty that would have taken Cardiff two scores clear.

Another James burst gave Scarlets hope before an important turnover from Lloyd stopped the home attack and halted any hopes of a dramatic home revival.

Replacements: McKee, J Morse, Hawley, Groves, T Davies, Hughes, Hawkins, I Jones.

Cardiff: Winnett; Beetham, Malan, B Thomas, Grady; Sheedy, Mulder; Sio, Belcher (capt), Sebastian, McNally, T Williams, Mann, D Thomas, Basham.

Replacements: E Lloyd, Barratt, Wainwright, Thornton, Botham, Bevan, J Evans, Millard.

Assistant referees: Carwyn Sion (WRU), Lloyd Edwards (WRU)

articles.title: Adam Jones: Former Wales prop sheds five stone in Cardiff half-marathon challenge
articles.summary: Former Wales prop Adam Jones will face one of his greatest challenges when he tackles the Cardiff half-marathon.
articles.body:
Former Wales prop Adam Jones achieved a lot in his glittering career as he became one of Welsh rugby's most recognisable cult heroes.

He is a three-time Grand Slam champion and a British and Irish Lions series winner, making 100 international appearances before retiring in 2018.

Jones will concede he was known for his scrummaging prowess rather than his running exploits.

Now aged 45, Jones will tackle one of the most significant physical tests of his life when he takes on the Cardiff half-marathon on Sunday, 4 October.

The Harlequins scrum coach has lost more than five stone (32kg) in his quest to "take himself out of his comfort zone".

Dropping weight and cutting out chocolate

Jones was inspired after seeing an image of himself when he was part of the Wales coaching staff in 2025, when he weighed in at 24st 7lb (156kg).

"When I was out in Japan with Wales last year, I remember the camera panning to me at the end of the tour and I was massive," said Jones.

"I thought I need to do something about this. I had a bit of gout, too."

Jones is typically dry and self-aware in his personal assessment.

"I've always been the type to look in the mirror and think I look like Arnold Schwarzenegger, when I'm actually far from that," he added.

"I'd go to the gym and do bits and bobs but my diet wasn't great and it was the old cliche of walking up the stairs being hard.

"I needed a challenge to change things."

Jones, who is running in aid of two charities, St David's Hospice Care and Prostate Cymru, has recently weighed in at 19st 7lb (124kg) which is close to his ideal playing numbers.

He admitted he had issues with his weight whilst playing, and recruited support from Wales chief Warren Gatland and fitness coach Craig White.

"When I was a player, I needed to be at a certain weight," said Jones

"I told Gatland and Craig, 'give me a weight and I'll stick to it'. If I was at that weight, I could play well.

"I'd often crash diet as a player. If I had a bad weekend, I'd get back to my ideal weight before the next match.

"It was stupid. But I don't need to be crash-dieting for Six Nations matches or Lions tours now.

"I've got a slow plan. Drop it down slowly and training every day in one form or another."

Jones admits he needed to change his diet.

"Chocolate has always been my weakness," he said.

"I've got a sweet tooth. So I cut that out, as well as bread."

Jones started slowly as he adopted the "couch to 5k" approach.

"As soon as I started doing it, I saw the benefit of the process. It was fascinating to see and develop week-to-week," said Jones.

"I enjoyed that and started ticking off the little milestones. It is a brilliant process.

"The first run was a five-minute walk, then a 90-second run, and so on. You're not going straight in and doing it.

"Once you've got that 5k, it was a sense of achievement and you get that buzz after running."

He took to his new sporting endeavour so well he soon upgraded his ambition.

"After that, I was thinking of doing a 10k, but then I saw Cardiff was long enough in the distance that I could train for a half-marathon," he added.

‘Weirdly, I enjoyed the running part of training, so it appealed to me.”

Jones recently did a 17km training run, not something he did during his 16-year rugby career.

"It's definitely the longest I've run," said Jones, who with typical humour went on: "If you added up all the distances I've run in Test matches, it probably wouldn't be far off that anyway!"

Jones says Harlequins players and coaches have been supportive.

"The boys have been brilliant," he said.

"A few of them have sponsored me. Some haven't, but that's mostly the big earners.

"I think they're waiting to see me finish first and then the money might go up a fair bit."

The former prop also believes it is a positive for the players to see him making the effort.

"I'm putting myself in a place where it's uncomfortable.

"I'm asking them to stay in the fight and stay in shape when it gets painful, so it felt wrong if they couldn't see me do the same.

"I do have perspective. It'll be hard, but there's harder things to do.

"I always tell the boys here you're not working down a mine. My grandfather was a miner. What he did was hard.“

Jones has not targeted a specific time for the half-marathon.

"People keep asking what time I want to get, it's more about getting around for me," he explained.

"I reckon there'll be a few other 19-odd stoners knocking around the same time as me, so we'll have a little race.

"I'm competitive but I'm fully aware I'm not going to win and made peace with it."

He also has added motivation courtesy of one of the Harlequins players.

"Cadan Murley put into ChatGPT the other day to see what time I should run it in and said if I beat that time, he'll give me more money.

"I'm happy with the time it said because if I can do it under two hours and 30 minutes, he will double the amount."

Jones will be supported on the course by his wife Nicole and daughter Isla.

His father might also attend with Jones admitting he is "glad to see me get off the couch and doing a bit".

"I am a little nervous about it, but I'm buzzing," said Jones.

"I've had the race number from the organisation and it means things have got real. I looked at that and thought, 'What have I done?'

"I might go incognito in the race so no one can see how slow I'm going, maybe I'll put a balaclava or a daffodil hat on, so I don't get abused!

"But I've heard good things about the event and how people support you. I'm hoping the Welsh public will get me around the last few miles."

Jones also hopes he might continue his running career.

"I'd imagine I'll want to try another half-marathon somewhere else after it," said Jones.

"But let's see how this one goes first before I start thinking about running across the Sahara Desert and world marathons and all that."

articles.title: Australia beat South Africa while down to 11 men in thrilling Test
articles.summary: Australia are reduced to 11 men but dig in for a remarkable win against a much-changed South Africa side as they beat the world champions 42-38 in Perth.
articles.body:
Tries: Ikitau 2, Donaldson, Wilson, Jorgensen Cons: Lonergan 4 Pens: Lonergan 3

Tries: Grobbelaar, van der Merwe, penalty try, van den Berg, Nche Cons: Pollard 2, Mngomezulu 2 Pens: Pollard

Australia were reduced to 11 men but dug in for an extraordinary win against a much-changed South Africa side as they beat the world champions 42-38 in Perth.

The Wallabies excelled with some vibrant attacking rugby, scoring five tries against the back-to-back World Cup winners to lead by 25 points with 16 minutes left.

But then a manic spell of four yellow cards in nine minutes left the hosts overrun, with South Africa mounting a comeback that ultimately fell just short.

The visitors made 13 changes after beating New Zealand in Baltimore but still fielded a strong starting XV, which boasted 240 caps in the second row alone.

But a year out from hosting the World Cup, and a year on from being soundly beaten on home soil by the Lions, it was the home side who impressed before their bizarre late collapse.

The teams traded early penalties before Springboks hooker Johan Grobbelaar drove over for the first try of the match after a powerful maul.

Australia responded well with a wave of pressure which was rewarded when centre Len Ikitau drove over from a metre out.

Ikitau then flew over for his second after the Boks made a mess of a high ball kicked through, but the lead lasted just three minutes.

South Africa played the ball quickly and flung it out wide with Edwill van der Merwe on the end of a stunning break to score in the corner.

The high level continued as the hosts took the lead again before the break. After 14 patient but quick phases, the Wallabies whipped the ball from right to left to find fly-half Ben Donaldson free to score in the corner.

The Springboks had strength in depth to call on, and coach Rassie Erasmus made all eight changes early in the second half with his side down by 10 points.

But it was Australia who continued to dominate. Captain Harry Wilson was denied a try as his foot was in touch but just seconds later he did burrow over the line close to the posts.

Wing Max Jorgensen then sprinted the length of the pitch to score a stunning solo score after South Africa fumbled the ball to make it 42-17.

Wilson was then sin-binned and South Africa finally got their first score of the second half with a penalty try, with Ryan Lonergan yellow carded as well.

The Wallabies were down to 13 and a crossfield kick found Van der Merwe in the corner but the wing dropped the ball before he could ground it.

Australia wing Joseph-Aukuso Sua'ali'i was then sin-binned as well to leave Australia three men down and replacement scrum-half Morne van den Berg scrambled in to cut the lead to 11 points.

Remarkably Australia then appeared to have scored again as Tom Wright intercepted a pass to run in - only for the try to be ruled out and Hunter Paisami shown a fourth yellow card for a dangerous tackle in the build-up.

South Africa had so much space and scored again through Ox Nche to cut the lead to four but time ran out.
