articles.title: WXV: Why latest defeat feels different for Wales
articles.summary: Wales may have suffered another Test defeat, but Sean Lynn's new-look side has given fans plenty to be optimistic about before next month's trip to Japan.
articles.body:
It was another defeat for Wales, but this one feels different.

As many of the three thousand-plus fans exited Cardiff Arms Park after the USA claimed a 26-24 victory, I assume we did so with a sense of optimism rather than the doom and gloom that often surrounds Welsh rugby.

What head coach Sean Lynn and his backroom staff have done to this group in just six weeks of pre-season is to be applauded.

Wales have been transformed from a side which whimpered out of a winless World Cup and Six Nations into a competitive 80-minute team and one the nation can truly get behind.

Speaking earlier this month, the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) women's rugby director, Nadine Griffiths, said the WXV series would be the real "litmus test" and a "brilliant opportunity to test our progress".

She would have been delighted with the way they obliterated a powerful South Africa side before going toe-to-toe against a USA team ranked inside the world's top six.

Teary-eyed players were naturally disappointed to lose by two points, but it is a sign of the higher standards this group now holds themselves to, and a sign of things to come before they head out to Japan for two further Tests in October.

USA edge past Wales in WXV with Tafuna hat-trick

As it happened: USA earn slender WXV series win over Wales

Wales hooker Kelsey Jones said the players were "disappointed and frustrated" with Saturday's result.

"We left loads out there. Credit to the USA, they were class, but I also think a lot of their success came from our mistakes," she said.

"The girls put in such a shift every week and they are absolutely class. We want to go out, we want to play rugby, that's the most exciting part. We're playing a brand of rugby that we haven't seen from a Wales team in a while.

"It's now about the little fixes, and we've got a big few weeks leading into Japan. Hopefully you've seen that change in the performances."

Wales co-captain Kate Williams said the "overall feeling was just gutted".

"The Test match was there for the taking," she added. "But when we're making that many errors in the championship minutes at the end of the game, we're never going to come out on top.

"We're in these Test matches and we believe that we can win these Test matches. It's going to come right from us. We're going to learn and the next time this happens, it's not going to end like this."

Lynn said "you can see the squad that is building", pointing to his inspirational co-captains Alex Callender and Williams, the discovery of Amy Williams on the wing and Keira Bevan's ability to play at 10.

Young forwards Branwen Metcalfe and Bryonie King have also displayed their Test pedigree, while mainstays such as Georgia Evans, Lisa Neumann and Sisilia Tuipulotu are playing with renewed confidence.

"It's a stable coaching team that we've got now, Gareth Harris coming in as S&C [strength and conditioning]; we've just got to believe in the process," said Lynn.

"I definitely know that we're a lot more competitive and we're being more clinical when we are in those 22 areas."

The reaction of former Wales internationals has also been positive in defeat.

Speaking on BBC One, Philippa Tuttiett said: "Wales were on a run of nine international defeats.

"The turnaround that they have done to beat South Africa and push the sixth-ranked team in the world to the end is incredible.

"It was a tough innings, but still a really proud performance."

Dyddgu Morgan-Hywel said: "We did see the momentum from the South Africa win.

"I was a little worried, but Wales put another performance in. Yes, they're disappointed, but there was only two points in it."

Former captain Siwan Lillicrap said: "I was stood up in commentary and I felt gutted and proud all at the same time.

"I was gutted because they stayed in the fight and could have won it, and proud of the fight they had.

"There were errors; Test match rugby isn't always going to be perfect, but you've got to remember USA are sixth in the world.

"They had an outstanding performance last week, but you learn when you win and you learn when you lose.

"We're still seeing really good stuff and growth from what we've seen previously."

Wales will have a well-earned week off now before returning to camp to prepare for their mini tour of Japan.

They will play two Tests against the Sakura Fifteen; the first in Tokyo on 24 October and the second in Kumagaya City on 31 October.

Wales have won both of their two previous meetings against Japan, who are ranked one place below them in 12th.

But with the humidity and travel to contend with, Wales will have to keep showing signs of progress if they are to continue their upward trajectory - and not only meet the standards they now demand of themselves, but also what we too have come to expect.

"I was gutted because they stayed in the fight and could have won it, and proud of the fight they had.

"There were errors; Test match rugby isn't always going to be perfect, but you've got to remember USA are sixth in the world.

"They had an outstanding performance last week, but you learn when you win and you learn when you lose.

"We're still seeing really good stuff and growth from what we've seen previously."

Wales will have a well-earned week off now before returning to camp to prepare for their mini tour of Japan.

They will play two Tests against the Sakura Fifteen; the first in Tokyo on 24 October and the second in Kumagaya City on 31 October.

Wales have won both of their two previous meetings against Japan, who are ranked one place below them in 12th.

But with the humidity and travel to contend with, Wales will have to keep showing signs of progress if they are to continue their upward trajectory - and not only meet the standards they now demand of themselves, but also what we too have come to expect.

articles.title: Ireland 31-24 Japan: Beibhinn Parsons becomes record try scorer as Ireland beat Japan
articles.summary: Beibhinn Parsons becomes Ireland women's all-time record try scorer as they hold off a late comeback from Japan to register a 31-24 win in the WXV Global Series at Dexcom Stadium.
articles.body:
Tries : Hogan (2), Parsons (2), Dalton Cons : O'Brien (3)

Tries : Nagaoka (2), Nagata, Asari Cons : Nishi (2)

Beibhinn Parsons became Ireland women's all-time record try scorer as they held off a late comeback from Japan to register a 31-24 win in the WXV Global Series at Dexcom Stadium.

Tries from Brittany Hogan and Parsons gave the home side the lead after a dominant first half.

Japan looked strong after the restart before Parsons registered her 24th Test try to take the scoring record and help them secure the win.

Scott Bemand will be happy with his side's response after they let a 19-point lead slip away against the USA in their WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium.

Ireland 'showed what we're about' in Japan win

Both sides had to navigate a strong wind in Galway, and it was Ireland who adjusted to the challenging conditions the quickest with Hogan showing great persistence to cross from close range after 10 minutes.

It was a scrappy first half with plenty of stoppages and neither side able to carve open the opposition's defence.

Hogan once again showed her threat and extended Scott Bemand's side's lead when she finished a nice move from Aoibheann Reilly after the half-hour mark.

A mistake in the Ireland defence then gifted Japan a great opportunity to register their first try before Anna McGann rushed back to stop Nami Asari's run.

The home side extended their lead after a superb solo run from Parsons in her home town on 37 minutes.

Following captain Erin King's yellow card, Japan scored a late first-half try when Moe Nagaoka crashed over.

Japan started the second half brightly and Nagaoka crossed from a maul to narrow Ireland's lead.

Unlike against the USA, Bemand's side responded well to the setback and Aoife Dalton touched down just minutes after coming off the bench.

The end-to-end nature of the match continued with Japan continuing to push and Nijiho Nagata able to register Japan's third try from a maul.

Parsons then produced another impressive run after connecting with McGann's pass, with O'Brien able to add the extras.

In the closing stages, Asari narrowed Ireland's lead after the home side had originally done well to stop the visitors from crossing, but Japan could not produce an impressive late comeback.

articles.title: Australia 42-38 South Africa: Wallabies finish with 11 men but hang on for victory in extraordinary Perth Test
articles.summary: Australia beat the world champions in a one-off Test at Perth Stadium after losing four players to the sin bin inside the closing quarter; South Africa scored three late tries to cut a 25-point deficit to four; Les Kiss remains unbeaten in five Tests as Wallabies head coach
articles.body:
Italian referee Andrea Piardi reached for his pocket four times in the space of eight minutes, at one stage speaking to his television match official by mobile phone after the communication equipment failed as the Springboks scored three times to turn a 25-point deficit into a four-point one.

Harry Wilson went first, binned in the 69th minute for a high tackle following a video review. Ryan Lonergan followed two minutes later for diving into the back of a ruck, with South Africa awarded a penalty try for the professional foul.

Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii was next, ruled offside on review after a Springboks try had been disallowed. Hunter Paisami then went for a high tackle in the build-up to a Tom Wright interception try that was itself overturned, a score that would have put Australia 47-31 clear in the 76th minute.

Instead, the Wallabies were left with 11 men defending an 11-point lead and four minutes to survive.

Replacement prop Ox Nche crossed in the last minute to bring it back to four. South Africa had time for one more push before the clock ran out on them.

"It was a crazy last 10 minutes," said Wilson. "But that first 70 minutes, the way we played, we implemented our game plan. We did exactly what we wanted."

Australia head coach Les Kiss, who has now won all five of his Tests in charge, described the finish as "bizarre".

He added: "In those moments, you've just got to hold your nerve and stay clear about what you want to do and I think they did that.

"But I don't want us to forget about the first 60. I think it was a really important step up for us to take that game forward, control the game and really be brave and attack the game."

South Africa had started far better, Johan Grobbelaar's converted try and a Handre Pollard penalty putting them 10-3 up inside 10 minutes.

Centre Len Ikitau turned the game in the hosts' favour, scoring in the 23rd minute and again in the 27th, and although Edwill van der Merwe crossed on the half-hour, Ben Donaldson's try before the interval sent Australia in 24-17 ahead.

Wilson added a fourth before Max Jorgensen pounced on a Springboks mistake and ran 60 metres in the 64th minute to make it 42-17.

It was South Africa's first Test since they won the Greatest Rivalry series against New Zealand 3-1, and Rassie Erasmus made 13 changes to the side that beat the All Blacks 43-28 in Baltimore a fortnight ago, with only Eben Etzebeth and Ethan Hooker keeping their places.

"They capitalised on all our errors and I think discipline let us down, especially in that first half," said Springboks skipper Andre Esterhuizen. "We let them in too many times and that really hurt us."

Lonergan finished with 17 points from four conversions and three penalties as Australia held on for a memorable victory.

articles.title: The Prem: Leicester Tigers 38-40 Saracens - Rotimi Segun double seals Sarries win
articles.summary: Saracens overcome a second-half red card for Nick Isiekwe to begin the Brendan Venter era with a 40-38 win at Leicester Tigers.
articles.body:
Tries: Kata, Hamer-Webb 3, Radwan, Thompson Cons: Searle 4

Tries: Gonzalez, Elliott, Daly, Earl, Segun 2 Cons: Burke 5

Saracens overcame a second-half red card for Nick Isiekwe to begin the Brendan Venter era with a seesaw 40-38 win at Leicester Tigers.

Two tries from wing Rotimi Segun with Sarries short-handed saw the visitors prevail in a breathless 12-try affair at Welford Road.

Gabriel Hamer-Webb scored a hat-trick for Leicester, but it was to no avail as Venter's second stint in charge at Saracens got away to the perfect start.

Venter's colourful first spell in charge brought a series of disciplinary run-ins, but set the foundations for the success that followed under Mark McCall.

The loss of Isiekwe in the 54th minute for a 20-minute high tackle on Freddie Steward looked like it could be crucial as the Tigers took the lead for the first time through Adam Radwan's try.

Sarries were back up to 15 when Eoghan Clarke replaced Isiekwe after his 20-minute punishment was up, but by this time Segun had already restored their lead and they held on to win.

It was the fourth away win out of five on the opening weekend of The Prem season and the resilience Saracens showed in clinching it bodes well for the campaign ahead.

They have not made the play-offs for the past two seasons but they have made some smart signings over the summer, including Wales scrum-half Tomos Williams, who was man of the match.

Gloucester shock Exeter for superb victory

Bristol start with steely victory at Sale

Saints begin title defence with win over Newcastle

Saracens got out of the blocks fast with two converted tries in the opening 10 minutes from Argentina flanker Juan Martin Gonzalez - making his 50th league appearance - and Tobias Elliott.

Leicester hit back with two of their own from the powerful Solomone Kata, who shrugged off Elliott's attempted tackle, and Hamer-Webb after a lovely ball by Steward.

With Saracens employing a 6-2 bench split, the loss of centre Olly Hartley early on to an arm injury and the temporary removal of Tobias Elliott to an HIA, meant England flanker Ben Earl was sent on as a centre.

But it made little difference to Saracens' fluid attack with Elliot Daly, back after a broken arm, crossing out on the left after some lovely interplay.

Leicester responded in the second half with two more tries from Hamer-Webb, both involving impressive new signing Aaron Wainwright in the build-up.

In between Earl, in a more familiar back row role after the withdrawal of Alfie Barbeary at half-time, thundered over for Saracens from Williams' flat pass.

Leicester took the lead after a nice piece of vision from scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet with a deft chip through for Radwan to score. And as Billy Searle was lining up the conversion, referee Ian Tempest reached for a 20-minute red card after Isiekwe's shot on Steward in the build-up.

But 14-man Saracens regained the lead with a try from wing Segun after a pinpoint cross-kick by Daly, and after Leicester replacement James Thompson had burrowed over to restore the Tigers lead, Segun struck again wide out on the left with seven minutes left.

'We gave the ball up too cheaply' - reaction

Leicester Tigers head coach Geoff Parling told BBC Radio Leicester:

"I thought we did some good things, I thought we worked hard, but essentially we were too inaccurate and we failed to back up pressure moments when we had other opportunities.

"I think we turned over the ball 17 times to their 11 and in the end I think that told.

"The attack was good when we went hard and went through them first. We carried hard and cleaned out and did the basics well and that opened up gaps for Jack (van Poortvliet) and opened up gaps on the edges.

"But on the same side I thought in attack we gave the ball up too cheaply and too early and that actually hurt us."

"The boys very calmly worked out what to do - Elliot Daly played four positions today and did very well in all of them.

"Then you get hit with the 20-minute red card at a place like this, where it's been tit-for-tat.

"If you want to be in the top four, you've got to be able to keep your cool, work things out and I think in the last six or seven minutes - where we had 15 men and they had 14 men - were crucial.

"The adversity bit would be front and centre of what we're pleased with."

articles.title: Women's Super League Grand Final: Wigan 6-8 York Valkyrie
articles.summary: York Valkyrie become the first side to win the Women's Super League three times after an incredible defensive effort thwarts favourites Wigan.
articles.body:
Betfred Women's Super League Grand Final

York Valkyrie became the first side to win the Women's Super League three times after an incredible defensive effort thwarted Wigan Warriors at the Brick Community Stadium.

Under siege for much of a scoreless second half, York stood firm to claim a surprise win over the favourites.

Teenager Amelie Lenham, the player of the match, led the way with a series of crucial interventions as a first-half try from Sinead Peach, plus two goals from Ellie Williamson, proved just enough.

Wigan - who had their only try-scorer Mia-Jayne Atherton and Eva Hunter sin-binned in the first half - were left stunned after an uncharacteristically error-strewn display.

York head coach Leon Pryce felt Hunter should have been sent off for a forearm to the throat of Williamson as she carried the ball into contact but in the end it did not affect the result.

The Valkyrie, the only team to have beaten Wigan this season, dug deep into their well of resolve to shade a gripping Grand Final.

Without the influential Tara Jane Stanley through concussion, they were odds against but with Wigan unable to get into their free-flowing stride, York's superb determination saw them over the line.

They had a simple gameplan and played it to perfection.

Peach gave them a ninth-minute lead, spinning through the Wigan defence close to the line after making the initial break as they dominated the opening exchanges.

Atherton pulled Wigan level in the 18th minute after a fine break from Jenna Foubister. But she was then sin-binned for her part in a dangerous double tip tackle with Bethan Dainton on Jas Bell, and Williamson put over the penalty to restore York's lead.

Lenham went close to increasing it and Liv Wood was held up over the line just after the break but from then it was one-way traffic.

But York, winners in 2023 and 2024, simply refused to yield.

Lisa Parker, who played with a broken hand, made 47 tackles. Her fiance proposed to her on the touchline afterwards. She said yes. It was that sort of night.

York Valkyrie's Agnes Wood told BBC Radio York:

"That was incredible. All the girls worked so hard. It was massive from everyone.

"In the second half Wigan really gave it back and the biggest thing we had to do was scramble and make sure that they didn't score. That was the main aim of the second half.

"We were all really motivated by the fact that nobody was giving us any credit and we really wanted to prove everyone wrong. We didn't have the strongest start to the season, but have we proved everyone wrong?

"All the coaching staff have backed us 100% from beginning to end and they just said to keep going and keep going and we have and I'm just so proud of all the girls. They've put in so much work throughout the whole season."

articles.title: York Valkyrie hold out to beat Wigan Warriors 8-6 and win the Women's Super League Grand Final at Brick Community Stadium
articles.summary: With a superb defensive effort York Valkyrie hold out to beat Wigan Warriors 8-6 and win their third Women's Super League Grand Final; watch Warrington vs Wakefield in the Super League Grand Final live on Sky Sports Main Event
articles.body:
It was York's third title after previous victories in 2023 and 2024.

Early on in this year's final at the Brick Community Stadium, Sinead Peach went over to score the opening try, with Ellie Williamson providing the conversion.

Wigan came back to level the game in the first half as Jenna Foubister put Mia-Jayne Atherton through to score the try and Isabel Rowe converted.

Atherton was sent to the sin bin as was Wigan's Eva Hunter. The latter was fortunate to evade a red card for a dangerous tackle on Jas Bell. She was sin-binned and Williamson landed the decisive kick to put York two points ahead. It was a lead they would not relinquish.

Valkyrie continued to threaten with Amelie Lenham coming close to scoring and Liv Wood being stopped just short of the line after half-time.

Wigan launched attack after attack in the second half but, in a superb defensive effort, York held out, with player of the match the teenage Lenham standing out with try-saving tackles.

Afterwards as York celebrated becoming the first team to win the Women's Super League three times, the fiancé of Lisa Parker, who'd played with a broken hand, proposed to her, capping off a fairy-tale evening.

The game marks the conclusion of the Betfred Women's Super League season, with Wigan's Jenna Foubister, Eva Hunter and Megan Williams all in the running for the 2026 Woman of Steel Award which will be announced at the Rugby League Awards night in Manchester on Tuesday.

articles.title: The Welsh players that started strongly in URC and Prem
articles.summary: The talking points as Dragons draw, Ospreys lose and Cardiff take the derby bragging rights against Scarlets on the opening weekend of the URC.
articles.body:
The Welsh men's rugby season is back, with mixed results for the four professional sides.

Cardiff triumphed against Scarlets in the opening United Rugby Championship (URC) Welsh derby, draw specialists Dragons again shared the spoils, while Ospreys came unstuck in South Africa but did claim a four-try bonus.

Welsh exports in England made the headlines in the Prem, with Gloucester new boys Dewi Lake and Jac Morgan demonstrating what Ospreys were missing.

BBC Sport looks back at the opening URC weekend and casts an eye on the Welsh players starring in England's top flight.

Cardiff grind out victory in underwhelming derby

Anybody hoping for a rip-roaring Welsh derby to kick-start the new season in front of a full house would have been disappointed at what was served up in Llanelli as Cardiff defeated Scarlets.

It proved an underwhelming occasion, not helped by the late kick-off time on a Saturday evening with the official attendance given at just above 7,000.

There was the odd fleeting moment, like Blair Murray's superb solo Scarlets' try, Sam Lousi's outlandish flick pass and Cardiff fly-half Callum Sheedy popping up with an audacious and cheeky second-half header, but they were few and far between.

Cardiff were content with an away victory as they aim to again be the top Welsh side in the URC.

"I would have taken this before the game," said Cardiff head coach Corniel van Zyl. "These derbies are always close, and it could have gone either way.

"It had that first game of the season feeling where you find out where you are, so to come away with the win carries on the momentum from last season."

Number eight Taine Basham was named player of the match as he impressed after an encouraging finish to the previous campaign, while lock Teddy Williams was prominent in his first Cardiff appearance in almost a year.

"Taine has been tracking well, and we are excited about what he can do this season," said van Zyl.

"I'm pleased for Teddy personally because he had a massive injury. He had a comeback for Wales in the summer and had a decent start to this season."

Cardiff host Zebre on Friday night when they will again be without wing Josh Adams, who has still not recovered from the calf injury suffered while on Wales duty in the summer.

James shines as Scarlets slip at home to Cardiff again

It was not the start Scarlets wanted after finishing 14th in the URC last season.

They scored two excellent tries through Joe Roberts and Murray but paid the price for conceding three scores from driving line-outs.

"There was plenty of effort and endeavour, particularly in that first half where we looked like the team we trained to be," said Scarlets director of rugby Nigel Davies.

"We need to see more of those moments. Some errors started to creep into our game, particularly in the second half.

"Cardiff took their tries well, but didn't have to work hard for them. It was more about our mistakes, and we gave them three entries into the 22 where they scored."

Scarlets were missing injured key trio Sam Costelow, Taine Plumtree and Fletcher Anderson, with 20-year-old forwards Will Evans and Osian Williams making their first league starts.

"We had a team strong enough to go and win," said Davies.

"We've exposed young players and in the main they did well and will be better for this, we've got quality to come back."

Positives include the defensive effort of captain Josh Macleod, who made 28 tackles, and Murray's running threat.

Eddie James impressed as an inside centre, rather than the outside centre position where he has been played by Wales.

"Eddie's a great rugby player and the debate will go on where he should play," said Davies.

"He can do a particular job at 12 and can also play 13. He can run hard and get gain line, but he is also a ball-player."

Two points gained at Benetton or two lost? That Dragons are even able to contemplate that question is largely down to the efforts of Thomas Young.

The flanker had a strong first season at Rodney Parade and made a super start to his second.

Dragons were forced into a back-row rejig after the early loss of number eight Evan Minto, and in Young they possess a multi-threat forward.

Young was a menace at the breakdown and also has the footballing skills to thrive in an attack that is noticeably looking to offload more.

They were the URC's worst in that department in 2025-26, with a total of just 51, but they racked up 10 in Treviso, with impressive Tonga wing Anzelo Tuitavuki to the fore.

But it was Young, who would have won more than four caps were it not for Wales' riches at flanker, that deservedly won man of the match at Stadio Monigo.

The stats - three turnovers, 15 tackles, four defenders beaten - do not do justice to a display in which the flanker produced big momentum-shifting moments.

There were eyebrows raised when the 34-year-old was signed from Cardiff on a three-year contract, but he shows no sign of slowing down.

In fact, Young will be pivotal for a Dragons squad that needs a collective effort to soften the blow of losing Wales number eight Aaron Wainwright, a talismanic figure.

The value of Dragons' draw at Benetton will be determined by how they fare on home soil.

They do not leave Wales for the rest of the first block of the season and must make that count, with Scarlets next up in Newport.

Ospreys have enjoyed some memorable wins in South Africa, but leaving Durban with a bonus point is not to be sniffed at.

The Welsh side famously beat Stormers in Cape Town in 2024 during the same season as they won at Lions in the Challenge Cup.

They also enjoyed away wins at Southern Kings and Cheetahs before South Africa's 'big four' joined the URC.

Ospreys never realistically looked like adding to their list of scalps against a Sharks side who look set to be stronger than the one that finished 10th in 2025-26.

But Mark Jones' squad showed tenacity to stay in the contest with a vital score by captain Sam Parry from a driving line-out with the final play of the first half.

That they ended with four tries was a good effort given that this was not Ospreys at their most creative.

They made six clean breaks - although last season's average was only seven per game - had one offload and ran for 179 metres. Sharks' tallies were 10, 11 and 454.

"When you have slow ball and the defence is waiting for you, it's difficult to be creative," said head coach Jones.

"The Sharks are a physical team, and we didn't get the speed of ball to be creative with it, and it was difficult to identify the space.

"When we got speed of ball, we looked dangerous in patches, but there were too many errors."

Ospreys will hope to be slicker if they are to repeat the four-try trick against Lions on Saturday in what looks to be an even tougher test at altitude in Johannesburg.

While Ospreys were losing their opening game, former players Lake and Morgan starred for Gloucester on their debuts in the away win at Exeter.

Lake celebrated his appointment as the new Cherry and Whites captain with two tries and a player-of-the-match display, while Wales international team-mate Morgan also made a big contribution to the impressive bonus-point 45-24 victory.

Wales wing Louis Rees-Zammit also made a telling two-try contribution in Bristol's 34-24 away win against Sale.

A raft of Welsh internationals were on display at Welford Road, where Wainwright made his Leicester debut alongside Test team-mates Olly Cracknell and Tommy Reffell in the back row.

Wainwright impressed as he created two of three tries for Wales wing Gabriel Hamer-Webb.

But it was Wales scrum-half Tomos Williams, featuring for Saracens for the first time since switching from Gloucester, who showed his class with a player-of-the-match performance in the away 40-38 victory.

articles.title: Nathan Cleary says 'I'll be back' after horrific injury rules him out of Rugby League World Cup
articles.summary: Nathan Cleary responds to the horrific injury that has ruled him out of the Rugby League World Cup by promising "I'll be back."
articles.body:
Nathan Cleary has responded to the horrific ankle injury that has ruled him out of the Rugby League World Cup by declaring "I'll be back."

The Australia great, 28, will miss the tournament in his home country after suffering a compound fracture and dislocation to his left ankle while playing for Penrith Panthers in their NRL play-off defeat by Newcastle Knights on Sunday.

Half-back Cleary - who helped Australia win the World Cup in Manchester four years ago - needed emergency surgery in hospital after being injured in a tackle by Phoenix Crossland.

Knights hooker Crossland was sent off for a 'hip-drop' tackle - which the NRL outlawed in 2020.

A hip-drop tackle is committed when a defender grabs the runner with both hands or wraps them with both arms, and then swivels or drops the hips or lower body, landing on and trapping the opponent's leg below the knees.

"Surgery done... Thank you so much to everyone that has reached out, the support has been unbelievable," Cleary posted on Instagram.

"Yesterday sucked but it's all part of the journey and it's made me even more grateful for the people I have around me. I'll be back."

Cleary had started Sunday's match on the bench because he was already carrying an injury to his right foot, which had a broken bone.

His father Ivan, the Panthers' head coach, said afterwards that his son would have surgery on both feet.

"I think that's why I was even more emotional on what happened to him, how hard he worked and what he put himself through to get himself to play today," the coach said.

Crossland was referred to the NRL Judiciary over the tackle, and is likely to receive a lengthy ban which would not only rule him out of Sunday's NRL Grand Final, in which Newcastle face Sydney Roosters, but may also affect his availability for New Zealand during the World Cup.

Australia will face New Zealand in the opening match of the World Cup in Sydney on 15 October (10:05 BST). The two teams are also favourites to face each other in the final, in Brisbane on 15 November (08:35 GMT).

articles.title: Prem talking points: Santi Carreras' try and Henry Pollock's hair
articles.summary: Old names, new looks and some stunning scores marked the return of the Prem for another season.
articles.body:
At the start of pre-season, at their St Albans training ground, Brendan Venter made a speech to his Saracens squad.

"I don't want to be competitive in this league," the returning director of rugby said. "I want to dominate."

Sarries were short of domination - the lead swapped hands four times in the final half hour of a blockbuster - but victory away at Leicester was a fine statement of intent.

Hobbled by an injury to Olly Hartley in the first half and then reduced to 14 men by Nick Isiekwe's 20-minute red card in the second, the visitors nonetheless dug deep and silenced the baying Tigers fans with an extraordinary 40-38 win.

"We've worked a lot more on our mental game, our ability to deal with setbacks, to keep sticking to our process when things don't go our way," Ben Earl, who was initially deployed in the centres in a rejigged backline, told BBC Radio 5 Live afterwards.

"Maybe a different Sarries team from the last couple of years would probably have dropped away in different points in that, but we kept fighting away and finding a way."

Since their return from the Championship, no club has racked up more regular-season Prem points over the last five campaigns than Saracens.

They haven't felt as consistent as that stat suggests though. They narrowly missed out on the play-offs in each of the past two seasons.

This year, they have been strengthened by signings; Tomos Williams crackled with cunning at scrum-half. But they also have a hugely promising generation of talent coming through.

Second row Olamide Sodeke, 21, came on and played his part in a massive front-five final-quarter effort.

Twenty-two year-old Nathan Michelow, part of the England's 2024 under-20 World Cup winning side, is pushing hard for a starting spot in a stacked back row.

If Venter can marry young, new and superstar existing talent, while rallying the squad around his belligerent belief, they will be hard to stop.

Saracens edge out Leicester despite Isiekwe red

You probably have seen it already. If you haven't, you really should. , external

The try of the round came 32 minutes into Bath's win at Harlequins on Friday night.

The hosts, only four points down at that stage, had a clear two-on-one 30m out down the left wing.

Quins' Tyrone Green made what he thought would be a scoring pass to Oscar Beard, only for Bath full-back Santi Carreras to lunge foot-first between the two.

The ball cannoned upwards, Carreras chased, gathered one-handed and raced in under the sticks at the other end.

An outrageous score, with an outrageous slice of luck presuming Carreras was gambling to get anything on the ball, rather than plotting that particular flightpath.

It is unlikely many will repeat Carreras's exact play. But more may start sticking a boot into the passing lane in similar situations, given the stakes involved.

Had Carreras gone with a hand and knocked on, he was likely looking at a penalty try and a sin-binning, given the lack of cover behind.

All that was at risk by going for a volleyed fly-hack was looking very silly had Green hung on to the ball.

Carreras magic lights up Bath win over Harlequins

Cherry and Bright as Gloucester make winning start

Gloucester's pre-season was not all forward-facing.

Brett Deacon and Joel Tomkins, brought in from Leicester and Catalan Dragons, as new forwards and defence coach respectively also used a bit of nostalgia to inspire their new charges.

Mike Teague, part of a gnarly 1980s Cherry-and-White pack, was among the club legends they channelled to explain the hard-nosed approach they wanted.

In winning away to Exeter, there was plenty of that grit on show. As there should be when you look down the teamsheet

Val Rapava Ruskin is one of the top-flight's best scrummaging loose-heads. He packed down alongside Dewi Lake, who put in a player-of-the-match performance on debut, and England prospect Afolabi Fasogbon. The second row consisted of Springbok Rugby World Cup winner Jean Kleyn and Arthur Clark, one of the league's best young locks.

Add in the energy and bravery of Jac Morgan, typically topping the turnover and tackle charts, Freddie Thomas's industry and Will Trenholm's old-school go-forward and there is a foundation there to build on.

Out the back there is a rat-pack set of bright young English-qualified things.

Seb Atkinson was immense. Will Joseph scorched past Immanuel Feyi-Waboso for a superb score. Ben Redshaw at full-back is eye-wateringly rapid. Fly-half Charlie Atkinson, all clever kicks and keen eye for a gap, has looked the part since switching back into 10 from full-back halfway though last season.

Chris Boyd, newly appointed as the club's technical director, previously moulded something special from Northampton's raw, local talent. You would forgive some in the Shed for dreaming big.

"The important thing is that it's not one and done for us," said Lake afterwards.

Quins at home on Saturday is next up and expectations have been raised.

Gloucester wanted to lay down marker - Lake

Gloucester shock Exeter for superb victory

With the upheaval and restructuring in Welsh rugby, the perennial talking point of turning the Prem into an Anglo-Welsh league reared its head over the summer.

Rob Baxter, Pat Lam and George Skivington, bosses of Exeter, Bristol and Gloucester respectively, are all positive on the idea. Perhaps predictably given their clubs' relative proximity to the border.

The opening day of this season showed that, in a large part, the Welsh are already here however.

Williams was excellent for Saracens, but Aaron Wainwright also made a fine debut, leading an all-Welsh Tigers back row of Olly Cracknell and Tommy Reffel. Out wide Gabriel Hamer-Webb, who made his Test bow against Scotland in February, scored a hat-trick for the hosts.

Louis Rees-Zammit scored two in Bristol's win over Sale. Lake also picked up a brace of scores - the first of which Dafydd Jenkins was unable to stop - as he impressed alongside fellow new boy Morgan in Gloucester's win over Exeter.

With Bath's Louie Hennessey, Harlequins' Bryn Bradley, Exeter's Kane James and Sale's Christ Tshiunza, there are also plenty of young guns to keep Steve Tandy's scouts crossing the bridge.

Bristol start with steely victory at Sale

The Welsh players who started season strongly

"It's not a gender reveal bro, you just got cornrows!"

Chunya Munga found the fuss , external caused by team-mate Henry Pollock's new haircut, marking his 50th Saints appearance in Friday's win over Newcastle Red Bulls, amusing.

After a summer of contract wrangling, Pollock kept his look hidden under a beanie and scrum-cap before emerging for kick-off and ensuring the spotlight stayed on him.

He is not the only rugby figure to have a makeover however.

South Africa boss Rassie Erasmus, and his coaching team, have shaved their heads this autumn after losing a bet with their players connected to the series victory over New Zealand.

Meanwhile Joe Marler, probably still edging Pollock in the crossover star stakes, has previously taken to the field with an advert for team-mate Olly Kohn's sausage company shaved into his head.

All-time rugby haircuts, good or bad? Feel free to comment below.

articles.title: England Women's Rugby League World Cup squad: Jasmin Strange earns first call-up
articles.summary: Australia-born second-row forward Jasmin Strange is one of four potential debutants in England's 23-strong squad for the World Cup.
articles.body:
Australia-born Jasmin Strange is one of four potential debutants in England's 23-strong squad for the World Cup.

Sydney Roosters second-row forward Strange, who is set to play in Sunday's NRLW Grand Final against Brisbane Broncos, has committed herself to England, for whom she qualifies through her mother Adele.

The 23-year-old is the daughter of Roosters women's head coach John Strange, who played for Featherstone in the 1990s.

Strange is joined by three uncapped players - Leeds Rhinos' Connie Boyd, Hope Millard of Canterbury Bulldogs, and Wigan Warriors' Lucie Sams.

In addition to Strange and Millard, three other NRLW players have made the squad - including dual code international Fran Goldthorp, who last played rugby league for her country at the most recent World Cup in 2022.

Newcastle Knights' Georgia Roche and Hollie-Mae Dodd of Canberra Raiders have also been included.

Strange's inclusion as a heritage player - one who qualifies through parentage - comes after eligibility rules were relaxed this year.

An International Rugby League ruling means that players can now represent more than one of the three tier one nations - Australia, New Zealand and England.

That led to speculation that Stu Barrow might call on more heritage players with NRLW experience - such as Roosters playmaker Jocelyn Kelleher, Bulldogs half-back Tayla Preston and Wests Tigers full-back Caitlin Turnbull.

But head coach Stu Barrow has said he wants to give homegrown players an opportunity to develop.

All three Woman of Steel nominees - Jenna Foubister, Eva Hunter and Megan Williams - have been selected, along with six of their Wigan team-mates. Grand Final winners York Valkyrie have one player in the squad in forward Liv Wood.

Loose forward Jodie Cunningham, who will retire after the World Cup, is selected along with St Helens team-mate Vicky Whitfield, who will be competing at her fourth World Cup.

Barrow said: "Narrowing our squad from 40 players to a final 23 has involved some difficult decisions, but we believe we have the right balance of experience and youth to compete on the world stage.

"It's also an exciting moment for the programme with the inclusion of Australian-based heritage players for the first time."

This year's men's, women's and wheelchair World Cups will run concurrently, with England competing in all three. The wheelchair squad was announced last week, while the men's squad will be confirmed on 5 October.

The tournaments are being staged largely in Australia, with Papua New Guinea's men and women each playing two pool matches in their own country, and their New Zealand counterparts playing one.

England face three group matches - beginning in Perth against Wales on 17 October and Australia on 24 October, before facing Samoa in Wollongong on 30 October.

The top two sides in England's four-team group with go through to the semi-finals on 7 and 8 November, with the final on 15 November.

articles.title: Fehi Fineanganofo: Newcastle Red Bulls agree deal delay
articles.summary: Free-scoring All Blacks wing Fehi Fineanganofo convinces Newcastle Red Bulls to delay his arrival on Tyneside so he can chase his dream of playing at the Rugby World Cup.
articles.body:
Free-scoring All Blacks wing Fehi Fineanganofo has convinced Newcastle Red Bulls to delay his arrival on Tyneside so he can chase his dream of playing at the Rugby World Cup.

It was originally announced back in January that the 24-year-old had agreed a two-year deal with Newcastle , beginning at the start of the current campaign.

However, Fineanganofo's exceptional form with the Wellington-based Hurricanes in Super Rugby then propelled him into Test reckoning.

He made his New Zealand debut against France in July.

Under All Blacks selection rules, a move overseas this year would have put Fineanganofo's emerging international career on ice and ruled him out of contention for the Rugby World Cup, which begins in October 2027.

Newcastle have therefore allowed Fineanganofo to stay with the Hurricanes, for whom he broke the record for the most tries in a single Super Rugby campaign this year, for an extra season.

His Newcastle deal is still for two campaigns, but now covers the 2027-28 and 2028-29 seasons instead.

"I'm really grateful to Newcastle Red Bulls for the support and understanding they've shown me," said Fineanganofo.

"The opportunity to stay in New Zealand and push for selection for the Rugby World Cup means a huge amount, and I'm fully committed to joining the club after the tournament and giving everything I can to the team."

Newcastle's sporting general manager Neil McIlroy said: "We are fully supportive of Fehi's desire to represent his country at Rugby World Cup 2027, which marries with our own philosophy of aiming high and enabling our athletes to achieve their ambitions.

"Fehi's arrival in 2027, with additional international experience that will only add to his already devastating qualities as a top-class winger, is another statement of intent around where this club is going."

The compromise ends long-running uncertainty about Fineanganofo's future.

In June, New Zealand Rugby denied they were attempting to put together a deal to get Fineanganofo out of his Newcastle contract.

Just a few weeks ago, Red Bulls' head coach Dan McFarland said he expected Fineanganofo to arrive in November and play in the current campaign.

His side began the Prem season with former Ulster man Werner Kok, signed in June as doubts over Fineanganofo's move increased, and 35-year-old Christian Wade as their first-choice wings.

McIlroy kept open the possibility of adding to the club's options in that position.

"We are more than happy with the quality and depth that our existing squad possesses, but may yet choose to add to the outside back position if a player of the required standard becomes available," he said.

Newcastle lost 59-26 away to defending champions Northampton on Friday in their league opener, and will take on Leicester at home on Saturday.

articles.title: Rugby League World Cup: History beckons for Wales' defiant Ffion Lewis
articles.summary: Ffion Lewis is relishing the prospect of donning the Wales kit while making history as the first woman from her nation to become a dual-code World Cup player.
articles.body:
Ffion Lewis is relishing the prospect of donning the Wales kit while making history as the first woman from her nation to become a dual-code World Cup player.

The 28-year-old played for Wales in union at the 2022 Rugby World Cup and heads to Australia for the 2026 Rugby League World Cup in October.

Having overcome a serious knee injury and dealt with the disappointment of not being offered the chance to renew a contract with the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU), Lewis says the last few years have "been very tough".

But having returned to the 13-a-side code with London Broncos, Lewis is "grateful" to be able to play in another World Cup.

"It's been a journey this last few years, been very tough, but I knew I had a goal in mind and didn't want to give up on myself, just having the opportunity to go out and play," she told the Scrum V Podcast.

"I didn't think I was ever going to still be in a position to wear a Welsh shirt, different codes [and] a very different path to where I thought I would be at this point in my career."

Bluck earns Rugby League World Cup call from Wales

Heroic York rearguard stuns Wigan in Grand Final

Lewis was part of the Wales squad at the 2022 union World Cup and was set to play in the inaugural WXV tournament a year later.

But she suffered a serious knee injury as Wales beat Italy in the 2023 Six Nations.

Since her recovery Lewis has played for Brython Thunder in the Celtic Challenge but, with no WRU contract, felt she had unfinished business and "didn't want any regrets".

"I could have easily just walked away from rugby at that point. I could have just been like 'I'm done'," said Lewis.

"But internally, I knew I wasn't, and I put so much time and effort into coming back and getting back fit, and I was only 28, and I was like, 'I've still got so much time left', and I just felt individually I didn't deserve my time to be done based on someone else's decision.

"So I took some time, and then I just set a goal to myself. If I got the opportunity to play rugby league, great.

"If I had the opportunity to play union, I wouldn't say no. But this opportunity came up, and I just grabbed it with two hands, and hopefully now it's paid off."

articles.title: Rugby Union: Dallaglio to sell 2003 Rugby World Cup winners medal after bankruptcy
articles.summary: Former England captain Lawrence Dallaglio is set to sell his 2003 Rugby World Cup winner's medal after being declared bankrupt.
articles.body:
Former England captain Lawrence Dallaglio is set to sell his 2003 Rugby World Cup winner's medal after being declared bankrupt.

The 54-year-old has put a number of items from his illustrious career up for auction including medals, trophies and caps.

The World Cup medal is expected to raise between £50,000 and £80,000 while in total the collection has an estimated value of £180,000.

Dallaglio was one of the stars of the England side that won the World Cup in dramatic fashion against Australia 23 years ago.

Other items up for sale include a British and Irish Lions cap, his 1993 World Cup Sevens winner's medal and a 2003 Six Nations Championship winner's medal.

During an appearance on The High Performance podcast , external earlier this month, Dallaglio spoke about his bankrupcy.

He said: "As a result of getting divorced, I was made bankrupt.

"I had some financial problems - I could've done things a lot better."

He also said he sought therapy after his divorce and bankruptcy left him wallowing in "self-pity".

The auction at Budd's , external in Northamptonshire takes place on 13 October.

articles.title: Otro campeón que se une a los deportistas que han subastado sus trofeos por caer en la bancarrota
articles.standfirst: El exjugador inglés Lawrence Dallaglio pone a la venta su medalla de campeón mundial y otros objetos debido a su situación financiera
articles.summary: El exjugador inglés Lawrence Dallaglio pone a la venta su medalla de campeón mundial y otros objetos debido a su situación financiera
articles.body: Medallas. Copas. Trofeos. O simples recuerdos de una vida dedica al deporte. Unos preciados tesoros, muchas veces con más valor sentimental que material, que se convierten en el último salvavidas al que se agarran los deportistas cuando sus finanzas se precipitan a la bancarrota. Lawrence Dallaglio, excapitán de Inglaterra de rugby, ha sido uno de los últimos en sacar a subasta varios objetos ligados a su trayectoria deportiva debido a su complicada situación económica. Gorras, trofeos y la medalla de campeón del Mundo de 2003 se pueden adquirir en la puja que Budds, especialista en Europa en artículos deportivos de colección, llevará a cabo el 13 de octubre en Northamptonshire. "Como consecuencia de mi divorcio, quedé en bancarrota. Tuve algunos problemas financieros. Podría haber hecho las cosas mucho mejor", reconoció Dallaglio en el podcast The High Performance. El exjugador inglés fue declarado insolvente en agosto de 2025, con deudas de casi un millón de euros contraídas con la Hacienda británica y con su exmujer, Alice, entre otros acreedores mencionados por la prensa británica. Los 22 objetos de Dallaglio que saldrán a subasta están valorados en un precio de salida de unos 210.000 euros. La medalla de campeón del mundo sale a la puja con un precio de 32.000 euros y la estimación de que llegue a venderse entre 58.000 y 93.000 euros. Entre otros trofeos, Dallaglio también pone a la venta sus medallas de ganador del Seis Naciones (2003), de la Premiership (2003, 2004, 2005 y 2008), de la Copa de Campeones (2004 y 2007) o de subcampeón del Mundo (2007). En 2018 Boris Becker sacó a subasta sus trofeos y diversos recuerdos de su carrera, incluyendo zapatillas, calcetines y camisetas, para saldar sus deudas. Un año antes fue declarado insolvente en 2017 por un tribunal de Londres. El objeto más caro fue el Renshaw Trophy que Becker recibió por sus triunfos en Wimbledon (10.000 euros). El exfutbolista inglés David James, en bancarrota, en parte, por el costoso divorcio de su esposa en 2005, se vio obligado en 2014 a sacar a subasta camisetas y balones de fútbol firmados, además de bicicletas, altavoces, televisores, máquinas de gimnasio, discos, un coche y una motosierra. Steve Finnan, campeón con el Liverpool de la Champions League en 2005 sacó a subasta parte de sus trofeos como la medalla de campeón de Europa, la camiseta de la final firmada y la réplica de La Orejona tras ver cómo su empresa inmobiliaria entraba en proceso de liquidación. El exjugador de los Colts en la NFL, Gary Brackett, subastó su anillo de la Super Bowl XLI, así como los del Campeonato de la AFC tras haberse declarado en quiebra. Tuvo que cerrar todos sus restaurantes en 2020. La declaración de quiebra estimó sus activos en 2 millones de dólares, mientras que las deudas alcanzan casi los 5,8 millones. El exnadador estadounidense Ryan Lochte, aunque no lo asoció directamente a problemas económicos, sacó a subasta seis medallas olímpicas de las 12 conquistadas en su carrera en 2022: tres platas y tres bronces logrados en los Juegos de Atenas 2004, Pekín 2008 y Londres 2012. Tres años más tarde, Lochte subastó tres oros olímpicos de los seis metales que le quedaban, los conseguidos en el 4x200 libre de los Juegos de Atenas 2004, Pekín 2008 y Río 2016. Acompañando las medallas hay tres banderas olímpicas firmadas por numerosos compañeros de equipo, incluido Michael Phelps.

articles.title: Jack Willis retains Top14 award and admits desire to play Test rugby
articles.summary: Jack Willis, who last played for England at the 2023 Rugby World Cup,  retains his award as the best player in France.
articles.body:
Jack Willis, who last played for England at the 2023 Rugby World Cup, jokingly challenged reporters to find him a way back into Test rugby after he retained his award as the best player in France.

Willis moved to Toulouse in November 2022 after Wasps went out of business, and was initially given dispensation to continue playing for England given the exceptional circumstances.

The back row won the most recent of his 14 caps in a pool-stage hammering of Chile, but, having opted to remain in French club rugby, has not been eligible for England since.

A long-standing policy restricts England selection to domestic-based players. It strengthens Prem clubs' ability to retain top talent, while England also benefit from increased access and control over their players.

Willis has been a huge success across the Channel. He was named player of the match in June's Top14 final win over Montpellier as he added a fourth French title to the Champions Cup crown he lifted in 2024.

Willis came top of a three-man shortlist for the Top14's best player for the 2025-26 campaign, seeing off competition from France and Bordeaux-Begles fly-half Matthieu Jalibert and Clermont-Auvergne's All Black Harry Plummer.

Willis becomes only the second player - after France captain Antoine Dupont - to retain the accolade.

The 29-year-old made his decision to stay at Toulouse, where his contract runs until 2029, despite knowing it would put him out of contention for an England spot.

"You know what you sacrifice," Willis said of his Test career.

"It's something I still want to do, but rules are rules."

Willis is now, in theory, available for selection by Ireland.

Three years have passed since he last appeared for England and, under World Rugby's 'birthright' rule, he could now represent a country which he, his parents or his grandparents were born in. Willis' grandfather was born in Belfast.

Ireland's strong preference for home-based players has been relaxed on rare occasions in the past with Jonny Sexton and Tommy Bowe continuing to play for their country despite moves to Racing 92 and the Ospreys respectively.

However, the likes of Simon Zebo have also found themselves excluded after heading overseas.

It is highly unlikely any compromise would be found that allows Willis to play for Ireland while remaining with Toulouse.

"I'm a quarter Irish, but they have the same rules as England," said Willis.

"You need to do some digging, that's your job, you find the way [around the rules]!"

articles.title: Red Roses: England to return to Sunderland for Women's Six Nations
articles.summary: England will return to Sunderland's Stadium of Light – the venue for their record-breaking Women's Rugby World Cup opener – for the 2027 Six Nations.
articles.body:
England will return to Sunderland's Stadium of Light - the venue for their record-breaking Women's Rugby World Cup opener - in their first home match of the 2027 Six Nations.

The Red Roses will play Scotland at the venue on 17 April.

It will be the first time they have played a home match away from a rugby-specific ground outside of a World Cup.

England drew 42,723 fans to the Stadium of Light for the 67-9 victory over the United States that opened the Women's Rugby World Cup in August 2025.

That attendance surpassed the 42,579 who watched the final of the previous edition as the Women's Rugby World Cup's biggest crowd.

The Red Roses subsequently smashed that mark again with an 81,885 sell-out for their final victory over Canada at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium.

England's 2027 Six Nations campaign also includes home matches against Italy at Northampton's DPD Stadium at Franklin's Gardens on 24 April and a final-round meeting against France at Twickenham on 15 May.

The venues for their away fixtures against Wales and Ireland are yet to be announced

"It was an amazing atmosphere to be a part of - one of the favourites in my career," England full-back Ellie Kildunne said of her previous visit to the Stadium of Light.

"I just remember the noise when we got off the bus and the amount of time the fans stayed behind afterwards. It was incredible. They really spurred us on that night.

"If the match with Scotland can replicate anything close to that night, it's sure to be another memorable occasion."

England are aiming for their ninth successive Six Nations crown.

Their preparations for the tournament will begin after they play two Tests against Canada and one Test against the United States on the away leg of their WXV Global Series campaign next month.

articles.title: Glasgow v Ulster: Irish province without trio of backs for United Rugby Championship game
articles.summary: Ulster will be without injured backs Michael Lowry, Aitzol Arenzana-King and Robert Baloucoune for their United Rugby Championship game away to Glasgow on Saturday.
articles.body:
Ulster will be without backs Michael Lowry, Aitzol Arenzana-King and Robert Baloucoune for Saturday's United Rugby Championship game against Glasgow at Scotstoun (17:30 BST).

Full-back Lowry and wing Baloucoune suffered concussions in the Irish province's 34-29 defeat by Edinburgh in their opening URC game of the 2026-27 campaign.

Winger Arenzana-King picked up a knee injury during the game in Belfast, from which Ulster emerged with two bonus points.

All three players started last weekend's fixture, with Lowry captaining the side and scoring the first of Ulster's four tries in a match which Richie Murphy's side's comeback fall short after they bounced back from a 34-5 deficit.

Glasgow began their season with an impressive 26-20 victory on the road at Munster.

"Everyone was really disappointed with how we played at the weekend but I think the glimpse of 20 minutes of really good rugby was what we were expecting to bring," Ulster head coach Richie Murphy told BBC Sport NI's Mark Sidebottom.

"Yesterday we started our review and the things that we got wrong. We know we are a lot better than that we produced at the weekend.

"This week we have a really tough assignment away to Glasgow but it's really important that we turn the page here and try and right some of the wrongs that were in that game.

"Starting with getting our breakdown right, getting our defensive line coming forward and making sure we're connected. You've got to be at your best to get anything over there."

articles.title: Brendan Venter: Saracens face fines after director of rugby refuses media commitments
articles.summary: Saracens are facing fines from Prem Rugby for director of rugby Brendan Venter's failure to fulfil media commitments.
articles.body:
Saracens are set to receive a series of fines from Prem Rugby due to director of rugby Brendan Venter's failure to fulfil media commitments.

It is understood the club have already been handed a £5,000 sanction after Venter was not present at the Prem's pre-season launch day.

The South African also did not speak to the media before, during or after the opening-weekend victory at Leicester.

The Daily Telegraph reported earlier on Tuesday , external that Venter "resigned" as director of rugby last month and took up a new role of "head of rugby culture and wine consultant", with head coach Joe Shaw assuming responsibility for media commitments.

The report also claims Saracens asked permission in July for Shaw to front the club's media commitments.

However, none of this has been confirmed by the club nor Prem Rugby.

It is also thought a change of job title would not preclude Venter from his contractual responsibilities.

Saracens announced in January that Venter would be returning to the club as director of rugby and have yet to confirm any change to his day-to-day responsibilities.

He succeeded Mark McCall, who stepped down at the end of last season after 15 trophy-laden years in the job.

Venter's first spell as Sarries' director of rugby, which began in 2009, also included clashes with authorities over media commitments.

In September 2010, the club apologised to European Rugby Cup (ERC) officials for then-captain Steve Borthwick's failure to attend the Heineken Cup launch at Cardiff's Millennium Stadium.

Borthwick, now England head coach, was the only missing representative from the coaches and captains of 12 English, Welsh and Scottish clubs attending the event.

He had been told by Saracens to instead attend a team bonding session at a beer festival in Munich.

In December 2010, Venter himself was warned by European Rugby Cup officials for a post-match interview after his side's 24-21 Heineken Cup loss to Racing Metro, in which he repeatedly gave short answers, agreeing with whatever was being asked.

He later said it was inspired by a scene in the football mockumentary film, Mike Bassett: England Manager.

Venter left his full-time role at Saracens halfway through the 2010–11 season, to be replaced by McCall.

articles.title: Super League: Brad O'Neill named 2026's Man of Steel, Jenna Foubister is Woman of Steel in Wigan double scoop
articles.summary: Brad O’Neill named 2026 Super League Man of Steel and Jenna Foubister wins Woman of Steel; Wigan Warriors' Matt Peet also claims Coach of the Year honours; watch Super League Grand Final live on Sky Sports from 5pm on Saturday October 3 (kick-off, 6pm)
articles.body:
Wigan's men's head coach Matt Peet and women's head coach Denis Betts, meanwhile completed a great night for the club with both picking up Coach of the Year awards.

Combative hooker O'Neill had already claimed the Rugby League Writers and Broadcasters Association (RLWBA) Player of the Year awards, having helped Wigan to the League Leaders' Shield, the Challenge Cup and came within 80 minutes of the Grand Final.

With his tough-tackling, pinpoint passing and impressive durability, the 24-year-old has developed into an integral part of Peet's side. He saw off Warriors team-mate Adam Keighran and Leeds Rhinos' Lachie Miller to take the crown.

Foubister also overcame a couple of Wigan team-mates in nominees Eva Hunter and Megan Williams to be named Woman of Steel.

St Helens' Harry Robertson was named Super League Young Player of the Year for the second year running, with Leeds' Connie Boyd winning the Women's Young Player of the Year award.

Halifax Panthers' Rob Hawkins was named 2026 Wheels of Steel winner.

When and where is the 2026 Super League Grand Final?

The Grand Final is taking place on Saturday October 3, 6pm kick-off, live on Sky Sports , with the 'Theatre of Dreams' Old Trafford once again the host venue for the blockbuster event.

Starting back in 1998, the Grand Final has always taken place at the home of Manchester United (barring 2020 at Hull), with 10 different teams having competed for the trophy... so far!

Now that becomes 11 as Wakefield join St Helens, Wigan Warriors, Bradford Bulls, Leeds Rhinos, Hull FC, Catalans Dragons, Salford Red Devils, Castleford Tigers, Warrington Wolves, and Hull KR in experiencing walking out of the tunnel.

However, not all these teams have won it.

Indeed, only Wigan, Saints, Bradford, Leeds, and Hull KR have lifted the coveted trophy, with the rest of Super League daring to dream they can one day join that very small list.

We now know that one of Warrington and Wakefield will join those other five. Remarkably, it also marks the first ever Grand Final which has not included one of Wigan, Leeds, or St Helens.

How to watch the Super League Grand Final

The Super League Grand Final takes place at Old Trafford on Saturday October 3, live on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports+ .

The match will kick-off at 6pm, with coverage on Sky Sports from 5pm.

articles.title: Wigan hooker Brad O'Neill wins 2026 Man of Steel award
articles.summary: Brad O'Neill wins the 2026 Steve Prescott MBE Man of Steel award as Wigan's Jenna Foubister wins Woman of Steel.
articles.body:
Wigan Warriors hooker Brad O'Neill has won the 2026 Steve Prescott MBE Man of Steel, the first time he has been given the honour.

The 24-year-old England hooker beat his Wigan team-mate Adam Keighran and Leeds full-back Lachie Miller to win the award.

O'Neill has been at the heart of an impressive Wigan side which won the Challenge Cup and League Leaders' Shield in 2026.

He made 31 appearances in all competitions and was also named Rugby League Writers and Broadcasters Association Player of the Year.

O'Neill was sin-binned in last year's Super League Grand Final for a wayward tackle on Tyrone May, however he inspired Wigan to two trophies, after a season without silverware in 2025.

It was a memorable night for the Warriors with Matt Peet also named Betfred Super League Coach of the Year having guided his side to the League Leaders' Shield and Challenge Cup.

Wigan earned a clean sweep in the final three shortlist for the Woman of Steel award as Eva Hunter, Jenna Foubister and Megan Willams were all nominated, with Foubister taking the prize.

It was the second year in a row that three Wigan players were shortlisted, however this year the Warriors missed out on adding the Women's Super League title to their Women's Challenge Cup and League Leaders' Crowns after they were beaten by York Valkyrie on Sunday.

articles.title: Irish rugby: The international rugby 'trailblazer' and her legacy of cancer awareness
articles.summary: Rosie Stewart played for Ireland and was a founding member of Ulster Women's Rugby but died after being diagnosed with breast cancer.
articles.body:
They gathered to remember "a girl like no other" - a trailblazing rugby player whose exploits on the pitch were cruelly cut short by her death at just 33.

Last Saturday, on a sunny September afternoon two teams from two different corners of Northern Ireland came to City of Derry to contest the Rosie Stewart Memorial Bowl.

Stewart, from Londonderry, won four caps for Ireland between 1999 and 2000 and was a founding member of Ulster Women's Rugby but, in 2003, she died after being diagnosed with breast cancer.

The memorial match is held every year in her memory and also to promote female health, a cause her sister Colette Risely said would have been close to Stewart's heart.

"I think the more we do the talking, the more lives we will save," she said.

"Rosie would be the one to promote the awareness too if she could."

On Saturday, Stewart's former club Cooke, which contest the memorial match every year, took on Enniskillen in Stewart's home city, watched on by the likes of Collette, her father John Gallagher and husband Adrian, who said his wife was a "girl like no other".

But what was going on off the pitch was just as important, with a women's health discussion held before the match hosted by the Western Trust's Jacinta McCool and fitness coach Claire O'Hagan.

O'Hagan's spoke on female strength and conditioning and the impact of the menstrual cycle on athletic performance, while McCool focused on breast and cervical cancer awareness.

It was a "poignant" event for City of Derry player Kelly Gormley, who said a number of squad members have been affected by or had breast cancer.

"It's at the forefront of our minds," she said. "I think when you are delivering information and awareness, it's information you're taking to 20 or 30 girls."

Jacinta McCool, whose message of early detection of breast or cervical cancer leads to better cure rates, said it was important to raise that awareness.

"Hopefully anybody that hears one thing, they go off and tell three or four of their friends, then we are reaching a much bigger audience."

For Gormley, Stewart was a "pioneering" player in her efforts to grow the women's game.

"Why not celebrate someone from Derry who started the movement in women's rugby?" she said.

"She started a change for women to play rugby and so we are just marking that at our own club."

Speaking about the increase of women playing rugby in Northern Ireland, Gormley said she thinks Stewart would not be surprised about the growth.

"She was knocking down doors before people even knew about women's rugby, these rugby teams are growing really fast and it is a result of decisions she made and took," she said.

articles.title: URC: Callum Sheedy 'header' goes viral as Cardiff fly-half admits surprise
articles.summary: Cardiff fly-half Callum Sheedy says he did not realise his "header" against Scarlets in the United Rugby Championship (URC) game would go viral.
articles.body:
Cardiff fly-half Callum Sheedy says he did not realise his "header" against Scarlets in the United Rugby Championship (URC) game would go viral.

Sheedy headed the ball forward after chasing his own kick in the second half of the 21-15 victory against Scarlets on Saturday night.

The clip has had more than 800,000 hits across social media.

"I probably wasn't thinking at the time, that was the problem," said Sheedy.

"I remember the ball sitting up, and I could see Blair [Murray] coming towards me, and I thought it was going be an aerial contest.

"I thought there needed to be a way of me getting the ball past him, and there wasn't enough time to get it down to my foot, so the nearest body part was my head.

Sheedy said he was unaware of the appeal of the clip.

"I had a laugh, looking back at the video and the boys give me a bit of stick," said Sheedy.

"I didn't think of it at the time. After the game, I'd gone on my phone and my Instagram had blown up a bit. I'm glad people are enjoying it."

Sheedy says he was unsure whether using his head was allowed in rugby's laws, with former World Cup final referee Nigel Owens taking to social media this week stating he thought it was illegal if it was deliberate.

"I think it's a split 50-50 among the public," said Sheedy.

"I always thought it was legal, but enough people are telling me it's illegal, but who knows?

"Until the next person that does it, we'll never know."

Sheedy's exploits evoke memories of another former Cardiff maverick fly-half Mark Ring.

"I am waiting for Ringo [Mark Ring] to text me and I expect him to," said Sheedy.

"It would have been something he would have done."

Cardiff fly-half resources and home comforts

Sheedy played his part in the victory in Llanelli before being replaced in the second half by Jarrod Evans, who has returned to Cardiff from Harlequins this season.

With Ioan Lloyd, who is currently injured, also in the Cardiff ranks, head coach Corniel van Zyl has three Wales fly-halves to call on.

"All I can do as a player is try my best and perform the best I can," said Sheedy.

"We all want to be number one, so how we go about that is going to be challenging because we're all going to want to play.

"I'm sure it'll be healthy competition."

Cardiff return to the Arms Park to face Zebre on Friday night, where they lost only one home game last season.

"It does make a big difference," said Sheedy.

"Hopefully we get a big crowd because I remember last season there were a lot of close games, and in the last 10 minutes, the crowd got us over the line.

"Corniel speaks a lot about making the Arms Park a fortress and we managed that last season."

There is also expectation on Cardiff this season after their sixth-place finish in the 2025-26 campaign and qualifying for the Champions Cup.

"You've got to welcome that expectation," said Sheedy.

"We got in the play-offs, but the good sides back it up.

"I am confident in the squad. We had a great pre-season and good start to the season, so let's see if we can kick on."

Cardiff will name their side to face Zebre on Thursday and have back three injury concerns with wing Mason Grady (head cut) and full-back Cameron Winnett (head) both major doubts.

Wales wing Josh Adams is still missing with a calf problem, while Iwan Stephens and Theo Cabango are long-term casualties.

Wing Tom Bowen is line to come into the starting side for Friday with centre Harri Millard another option on the other flank, with Jacob Beetham able to switch to full-back.

articles.title: Sam Underhill: Bath and England flanker to miss Nations Championship with bicep injury
articles.summary: England and Bath flanker Sam Underhill is out for months with a ruptured biceps that requires surgery.
articles.body:
England flanker Sam Underhill will miss the Nations Championship this autumn after rupturing his biceps in Bath's opening Prem game away at Harlequins.

Underhill went off in the 48th minute of the win at The Stoop and was seen at the end of the game with strapping around his arm, which will require surgery later this week.

Bath expect the 30-year-old to be out until December or January, meaning he will miss a large portion of the domestic season as well as England's three internationals against Australia, Japan and New Zealand in November.

Bath head of rugby Johann van Graan said he knew straight away the injury was serious, which was why he went immediately over to Underhill when he came off the pitch.

"There are a few types of injuries where I just want to know straight away because I know the impact that it has longer term and I always feel for the players, so that's why I went straight down," Van Graan told BBC Radio Somerset.

"At the time I thought, we need to wait for a scan but this could be a biceps rupture. The scan turned out to be exactly that.

"He will get operated on on Thursday, that's a few months out of the game - not ideal from Sam's point of view."

Bath's Boxing Day game with Leicester moved back a day

Comebacks, fly-hacks and cornrows - Prem talking points

Underhill has been capped 51 times by England and played in all five of their Six Nations matches this year.

However he missed the summer internationals against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina to have an operation on a shoulder injury.

"It's always disappointing for every player when you get injured in a warm-up game, or round one, because you've just gone through a big pre-season," Van Graan added.

"Injuries are part and parcel of this game. Sam has had a few big ones. I'm sure he'll be back as soon as possible and [we're] looking forward to welcoming him back whenever that is, whether it's December or January."

Bath are also without new signing Jamie Bhatti after he broke a forearm during pre-season. Fellow prop Vilikesa Sela is out until November with a toe injury also picked up in pre-season, while wing Will Muir has no return date yet after injuring his shoulder last season.

Ben Spencer and Louie Hennessey are expected to return to team training in October.

articles.title: England flanker Jack Willis opens door to switching allegiance to Ireland
articles.summary: Toulouse flanker Jack Willis remains ineligible for England selection under the RFU’s restrictions on overseas-based players, but the back rower could qualify to represent Ireland and has hinted he would be open to playing for Andy Farrell’s side
articles.body:
The 29-year-old Toulouse back row has enjoyed another standout season in the Top 14, being crowned the league's Player of the Season for the second year running this week.

The Rugby Football Union (RFU) currently restricts overseas-based players from representing England, meaning Willis has been unable to add to his 14 international caps since the 2023 Rugby World Cup. He won his last cap during England's group-stage victory over Chile and remains under contract with Toulouse until 2029.

He was given a special dispensation to play for England at the tournament, having joined Toulouse in November 2022, after his former club, Wasps, entered administration.

The RFU has come under pressure to loosen the restrictions, and Willis had previously hoped the governing body would reconsider the policy .

The flanker is eligible to play for Ireland through his grandfather, who was born in Belfast, and could, hypothetically, switch allegiances to play for Andy Farrell's side.

It would be a huge coup for Ireland. But, like England, Farrell's side also has restrictions on overseas-based players, meaning prospective internationals must represent one of the country's four provinces: Munster, Ulster, Leinster or Connacht.

Willis has not given up on the prospect of playing Test rugby, and jokingly challenged reporters at this week's Nuit du Rugby in Paris to find a way around the rules.

"I'm a quarter Irish. But they have the same rules as England," Willis told The Telegraph and The Times .

He joked to reporters: "You need to do some digging, that's your job, you find the way [around the rules]."

World Rugby relaxed its international eligibility rules in 2021 , allowing players to switch national sides under certain conditions, including having a parent or grandparent born in the respective country and serving a three-year stand-down period from international rugby.

Willis has continued to impress for Toulouse since moving to the south of France and once again proved pivotal as the French club secured a fourth consecutive Top 14 title last season, scoring six tries and making 173 tackles.

Although he admitted he "missed" playing for England, Willis said it was his choice to continue his career in France.

"You know what you sacrifice," the flanker said.

"It's something I still want to do, but rules are rules."
